title: ”Opiskelijat eivät ole vain sisällöntuottajia vaan itse Ylioppilaslehti” – Ysälli voitti Ylkkärin ideakilpailun
content:
Ylioppilaslehden ideakilpailun voittajaksi on valittu Lumia Lammin ehdotus Ysälli. Voittanut työ rakentuu ajatukselle, että Ylioppilaslehden tärkein voimavara eivät ole sen verkkosivut, sosiaalisen median kanavat tai edes yksittäiset jutut, vaan opiskelijat itse.

Lammin mukaan opiskelijoita ei pitäisi nähdä vain lehden yleisönä tai satunnaisina avustajina. He ovat Ylioppilaslehden syy olla olemassa. Siksi Ysälli ehdottaa vuosittain järjestettävää ohjelmaa, jonka kautta opiskelijat pääsisivät mukaan tekemään journalismia, kehittämään uusia sisältöjä ja osallistumaan lehden toimintaan kokeneiden journalistien ohjauksessa. Ajatuksena ei ole perustaa pelkästään toimittajakoulua, vaan rakentaa yhteisöä lehden ympärille.

Ehdotus keskittyy kysymykseen, joka nousi esiin monessa kilpailutyössä: miten opiskelijamedia voi säilyä merkityksellisenä aikana, jolloin opiskelijoiden aika, huomio ja yhteisöt ovat hajautuneet yhä useampiin kanaviin? Ysällin vastaus on yksinkertainen: jos ihmiset kokevat lehden omakseen, he myös lukevat sitä, osallistuvat sen tekemiseen ja kertovat siitä eteenpäin.

title: Your home is their asset
content: Let’s be realistic, housing has always been a business. What has changed however, is its scale. By the end of 2024, the value of global real estate had reached 393 trillion USD (€379 trillion) according to Savills Research real estate analysis. Most of this value came from residential property. This is more than the combined value of all global stocks and debt, and 20 times the value of all the gold ever mined. The market is not driven by what Barbara Steenbergen, the EU representative of the International Union of Tenants (IUT), calls “small amateur landlords”, but by large investment and pension funds. These funds are often registered in one country but source capital globally, Manuel Aalbers, professor of human geography at KU Leuven, told The European Correspondent (TEC). “They might have Spanish or German names, yet the money they invest comes from the City of London or Wall Street.” Listed real estate funds, which account for only a fraction of the market, owned €199 billion worth of property in the EU in 2024, up from just €5 billion in 2004. title: Convention on Biological Diversity. What you need to know and why it matters
content:
You have probably heard of the UN Convention on Climate Change, which emerged from the Rio Earth Summit in 1992. What is less well known is that two further conventions were also born at the summit: the Convention to Combat Desertification, and the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). The three were always intended to be implemented together as humankind’s response to the global environmental crisis. The aims of the CBD, which has been ratified by almost every country on the planet, are the conservation of nature, the sustainable use of its products (for example timber from rainforests) and the sharing of benefits fairly by everyone.  

Every two years, states that have joined the CBD meet in a “Conference of the Parties” (COP), the global decision-making body that oversees implementation of the convention. This year’s meeting is the 17th – known as COP17. In 2022, in response to challenges including massive-scale deforestation and extinction-level declines in the populations of many species, CBD’s COP15 agreed the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework which sets out 23 targets for nature conservation.

title: Turkey and Azerbaijan: Old Allies Fall Out
content:
The close relationship between Turkey and Azerbaijan has been a reliable and longstanding feature of geopolitics at the often-disputatious junction of Europe and Asia.

The 2021 Shusha Declaration formalized a relationship that had provided Azerbaijan with the drones and other equipment to defeat Armenian forces in Nagorno-Karabakh the previous year. It extended Turkish influence into the South Caucasus and crowned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan as a powerful figure in the region.

Is that really now at risk from a dispute over girls’ schoolwear?

On 12 October, the Azerbaijani government introduced new school uniform regulations that effectively barred hijab-wearing female students from attending classes, triggering public criticism and protests in several schools. While authorities cited Azerbaijan’s constitutional commitment to secularism and its long-standing secular traditions, the decision has exposed deep societal divisions, with some segments of the public supporting the policy and others viewing it as a restriction on religious freedom.

title: DCA-sopimus etenee käytännön toimeenpanoon tavoitteiden mukaisesti
content:
Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen välinen puolustusyhteistyösopimus, Defence Cooperation Agreement eli DCA, on siirtynyt sopimusvaiheesta määrätietoiseen käytännön toimeenpanoon. Sopimus tuli voimaan 1. syyskuuta 2024, ja sitä on jo sovellettu Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen välisessä puolustusyhteistyössä. Samalla jatkuu yksityiskohtaisten menettelyjen valmistelu, jolla sopimuksen määräykset viedään osaksi viranomaisten normaalia toimintaa.

DCA on Suomea sitova kansainvälinen sopimus, joka luo ajantasaiset oikeudelliset ja hallinnolliset puitteet Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen puolustusyhteistyölle kaikissa turvallisuustilanteissa. Se täydentää Naton joukkojen asemaa koskevaa Nato SOFA -sopimusta ja tukee Suomen Nato-jäsenyyteen liittyvien velvoitteiden toimeenpanoa. Sopimus ei korvaa Nato-jäsenyyttä, vaan vahvistaa sitä kahdenvälisillä järjestelyillä, jotka mahdollistavat yhteistoiminnan suunnittelun ja toteuttamisen aiempaa sujuvammin.

title: Should AIPAC Register as a Foreign Agent? Zeteo Examines Pro-Israel Lobby's Influence on Elections
content:
The growing controversy over AIPAC’s impact on U.S. politics is the subject of a new Zeteo documentary titled Night Flower: Inside AIPAC’s Fight for Influence. The film examines AIPAC’s history and its role in shaping U.S. policy toward Israel, and questions whether its activities warrant further scrutiny under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, or FARA. “It says that you have to register under this law if you are acting at the request of a foreign government,” says Dion Nissenbaum, the filmmaker behind Night Flower: Inside AIPAC’s Fight for Influence. “And we talked to numerous people who showed us several examples of how AIPAC is acting at the request of Israel.”

Referencing the title of the film, Night Flower, Zeteo editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan says AIPAC “blossoms in the dark, shrivels in the light. We’re trying to put some sunlight onto AIPAC.”

title: Editing the Ethics of Care in Contemporary Art on Wikidata and Wikipedia: Artexte x Art & Feminism 2026 Wikiclub
content:
This year, Artexte, a library, research center, and exhibition space for contemporary art in Montreal has partnered with Art + Feminism to improve the coverage of the ethics of care in contemporary art on Wikimedia projects. The ethics of care emphasize reciprocity, interdependency, collective maintenance, and mutual support in art practices. This approach also provides an alternative perspective in contemporary art (and other sectors of society), where individual authorship and novelty are prioritized over maintenance work, such as preservation or repair.

Artists such as Mierle Laderman Ukeles have revindicated preservation, repetition, and repair as artistic practices. However, these practices often involve invisible labor that goes unseen or is undervalued, which is why focusing on care practices at the Wikiclub helps to highlight their importance in contemporary art. Care work–tasks that meet the needs of others–is also more often done by women and minorities, so highlighting it as a contribution on Wikidata and Wikipedia also helps address the gender and representation gaps on Wikimedia projects.

title: Preparing for the worst: a single attack could leave us without electricity or heating
content:
Delfi looks at the cyber threats already facing Lithuania’s energy sector and how it is preparing for possible attacks. On 29 December 2025, coordinated cyberattacks targeted more than 30 wind and solar power plants and two combined heat and power plants in Poland. According to CERT Polska, the country’s computer security incident response team, hackers managed to stop a steam turbine and a water treatment system at one of the plants. However, the heat supply to residents was not interrupted. The attacks on the wind and solar plants disrupted their communications with electricity distribution network operators, but power generation continued.

In July 2026, a cyberattack also affected the UK energy sector. According to British media reports, a small electricity generation facility was shut down for four days following the attack. On 7 September, the country’s Energy Minister, Michael Shanks, confirmed that the incident had affected a very small amount of electricity generation, but posed no threat to the wider UK energy system.

title: Housing: the basis of dignity and opportunities for all
content:
Housing is no longer just a local or national policy issue. Across Europe, housing costs increasingly shape people’s opportunities and influence the development of local economies. When people cannot afford to live where jobs are available, or young families struggle to find a home, the consequences extend well beyond the housing market. 

The scale of the problem is clear. Between 2010 and 2025, house prices in the EU increased by more than 60 per cent, while rents rose by almost 30 per cent. But the problem is not simply that housing has become more expensive. Across much of Europe, there is a structural shortage of affordable housing, alongside limited availability of social housing. 

The effects are visible across the economy. Workers find it harder to move to areas where their skills are needed. Young people are postponing leaving home, and families face growing difficulties staying in the communities where they have established their lives. What was once regarded mainly as a problem for low-income households increasingly affects the middle class.

title: NEW REPORT: Authoritarian Internet Controls Drive 16th Consecutive Year of Decline in Global Internet Freedom
content:
WASHINGTON, DC—Global internet freedom declined for the 16th consecutive year, with conditions deteriorating in 16 of the 38 countries assessed and improving in only 8, according to Freedom on the Net 2026: Seismic Shifts on the Global Internet, a new report released today by Freedom House. Authoritarian efforts to isolate populations from the global internet, expanding age checks for online access, and the weaponization of laws governing AI-generated content created new barriers to free expression and access to information. 

“Agentic AI promises to transform the internet,” said Freedom House Chief Executive Officer Jamie Fly. “Authoritarian actors are already weaponizing AI. We need to ensure that frontline activists and freedom fighters have access to cutting-edge technologies to counter these threats and to accelerate freedom in repressive societies. Democracies need to ensure that efforts to secure democracy and fundamental rights in the AI era do not restrict legitimate expression.”

title: Mohammad Azizi Remains in Detention and Legal Limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Azizi remains in detention.

A source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Despite the passage of 30 days since Mr. Azizi’s arrest, he remains in legal limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin. Some time ago, he was formally charged with propaganda against the regime on social media, disrupting public order and peace, insulting the Supreme Leader, and insulting religious sanctities.”

According to the source, despite his family’s efforts to secure his temporary release on bail, they have so far been unsuccessful.

On Wednesday, September 23, IRGC Intelligence agents arrested Mohammad Azizi at his residence in Alvand and transferred him to Choobindar Prison in Qazvin.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the specific actions underlying the charges against him.

Mohammad Azizi, a resident of Alvand, has previously faced arrest and judicial proceedings in connection with his activities.

title: Tajik Activist Given Lengthy Prison Sentence
content:
A court in Tajikistan has sentenced Asadullo Boboev, an opposition activist deported from Germany in June, to 17 years in jail. Human Rights Watch and other groups previously warned the German authorities that activists like Boboev could face mistreatment and criminal prosecution on politically motivated charges if returned to Tajikistan.

Boboev, 54, had lived in Germany with his family since 2017. He was involved in the Reforms and Development of Tajikistan movement, an opposition group critical of President Emomali Rahmon’s government. After Boboev was convicted under three articles of the criminal code, including “extremism through the internet,” a court sentenced Boboev on September 21, according to a media report. Tajik authorities have not published information on the case.

Boboev, who was deported from Germany on June 20, previously told media that Tajik authorities had opened a criminal extremism case against him because of social media posts criticizing the Tajik authorities. He said that the German court gave him until July 1 to prove that such a case exists, but he was deported before this deadline.

Suomen Madridin-instituutin galleriassa nähdään 28. lokakuuta alkaen kuvataiteilija Anni Kinnusen näyttely Strange Days. Madridissa esillä oleva näyttely koostuu uusista, vuonna 2026 valmistuneista teoksista sekä The Great Escape -kokonaisuudesta valituista valokuva- ja videoteoksista.

Anni Kinnunen (s. 1978 Oulussa) on kuvataiteilija, jonka valokuvataiteella on kiinnostavuutta niin valtakunnallisesti kuin kansainvälisestikin. Vaikka taiteilija esiintyy kuvissaan itse, ne eivät ole omakuvia. Kuvien hahmot edustavat ihmistä roolileikeissään, heijastavat aikamme tunnelmia ja taiteilijan mielialoja. Kuvaustilanteet ovat aitoja eivätkä kuvankäsittelyohjelmalla rakennettuja. Kuvat kuitenkin välttävät luonnollisuutta imitoivan kuvaston niin totaalisesti, että hänen kuviaan ei pidettäisi koskaan totena.

title: Smugglers Collected Up to $509M on Europe Routes in 2025
content:
Smugglers netted an estimated $388 million to $509 million from sea crossings to Europe in 2025, according to new research by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). The agency estimated that between 190,000 and 209,000 people were smuggled along four major Mediterranean and Atlantic routes, with criminal networks facilitating between 57 percent and 90 percent of departures. Fees varied widely depending on the journey, ranging from $170 for crossing to Spain’s Canary Islands to more than $7,500 for routes toward Italy and Malta, according to the International Organization for Migration.

The Central Mediterranean was the busiest route, with up to 100,400 people smuggled, followed by the Eastern Mediterranean with up to 51,300, the Northwest African Atlantic route with 33,000, and the Western Mediterranean with 24,500. These estimates, according to UNODC, reflect all smuggling attempts, including journeys that ended in interception or tragedy. The routes remained deadly: 3,404 people died or went missing in 2025, while another 104,200 were intercepted at sea and returned.

title: What Ancient Latin Sounded Like, And How We Know It
content:
Latin is a language

As dead as dead can be; 

It killed the Romans long ago, 

And now it’s killing me.

Latin is a language

As dead as dead can be; 

It killed the Romans long ago, 

And now it’s killing me.

That famed ditty isn’t likely to resonate with many modern school children, but interest in ancient Rome remains fairly robust. 

We’ve come to accept that those stately ruins were once covered in graffiti.

We can recreate their meals from hors d’oeuvres (Boiled Eggs with Pine Nut Sauce) to dessert (Pear Patina).

Thermae Romae, a popular Japanese manga-cum-feature-film, took us inside Emperor Hadrian’s bathhouse.

But what did the Romans sound like?

Kirk Douglas’ Spartacus? Or Laurence Olivier’s Crassus?

The HBO series Rome upheld the tradition of British accents.

Animator Josh Rudder of NativLang did a fair amount of digging in service of finding out What Latin Sounded Like, above.

(And he seems to have done so without the help of Derek Jarman’s NSFW Sebastiane, the only feature film to be filmed entirely in sermo vulgaris or vulgar Latin.)

title: Ballot Rejections Soared in Rural Counties After USPS Reduced Mail Service
content:
In early August, election workers north of Spokane, Washington, went across the street to the post office to check for late mail-in ballots. It was three days after the primary and they were expecting no more than a few dozen.

Instead, their mailbox was brimming with envelopes — more than 500 of them, each a vote that wouldn’t count. The sight was “jarring,” said Auditor Lori Larsen, a Republican who oversees voting in Stevens County.

Across the region, other election officials were getting similar jolts. In the 11 predominately rural counties in eastern Washington, nearly 2,000 ballots came in late, compared to about 600 in 2022, the previous midterm primary.

In recent weeks, concerns about mail-in voting disruptions have focused almost entirely on President Donald Trump’s now-shelved plan to sharply restrict who can vote by mail. 

But a ProPublica data analysis shows that delays resulting from the U.S. Postal Service’s cost-cutting measures have endangered the validity of ballots cast in rural areas, not only in Washington, but across the country.

title: Studiefonden delade ut drygt 1,2 miljoner euro
content:
Antalet ansökningar till Svenska studiefonden fortsätter att öka. Den här hösten har nästan 1 000 högskole- och universitetsstuderande inlett sitt läsår med hjälp av ett stipendium från fonden. Axel Österlund som studerar lantbruksvetenskap är en av dem.  Sammanlagt går drygt en miljon euro till studerande med svenska som modersmål eller studiespråk.

– Stipendiet från Studiefonden betyder för mig att jag kunnat fokusera på min praktik till hundra procent utan att behöva bekymra mig över min ekonomi, säger Axel Österlund.

Axel studerar lantbruksvetenskap vid Helsingfors universitet och fick ett stipendium för sin utlandspraktik i Kanada.

–  Jag valde att åka på praktik till Kanada för att få se hur en mjölkgård i Kanada skiljer sig från en mjölkgård i Finland. Mitt arbete består främst av att sköta om korna på gården, det vill säga ladugårdsarbete, säger Axel.

Axel är själv uppvuxen på en mjölkgård i Tenala, Raseborg, och har under 2026 tillbringat sju månader i Kanada. En av målsättningarna med praktiken var att lära sig nya saker inom branschen som han förhoppningsvis kan dra nytta av när han återvänder till Finland.

–  Till en sådan här grej underlättar ett stipendium massor.

title: Hackers launch ‘millions’ of attempts to exploit global PHP cyber flaw
content:
Cyberattackers have made “millions” of attempts to take advantage of a critical hole in a building block of the internet, a key cybersecurity provider said early Thursday.

Two top European cyber officials later told POLITICO that hackers have so far struggled to exploit the vulnerability.

Cybersecurity agencies worldwide continue to scramble to respond to the public revelation Wednesday of a flaw in PHP, a foundational computer programming language used to underpin 70% of the internet. 

Matthew Prince, the CEO of Cloudflare, an internet services company that is widely used by websites to block cyberattacks — giving it a high level of visibility over what hackers are doing — said in a post on X that it’s seen “millions” of “attempts to exploit” the flaw.

Cloudfare saw thousands in the 10 hours before the flaw was publicly announced, meaning information must have leaked, then tens of thousands in the 45 minutes after the announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and now millions, Prince said.

Amazon’s cloud division also said the flaw is “now being broadly exploited in the wild.”

title: Brazil’s election puts at risk country’s role as a bulwark against Trump interventionism in the Americas
content:
On Oct. 25, Brazilians will return to the polls for the second round of the presidential election. The results will matter not only for the future of country itself, but also for the region and the world. Alongside Canada and Mexico, Brazil, under the leadership of current President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is one of the few countries in the region that has stood up to Donald Trump’s meddling and interference attempts.

Under Lula, Brazil still serves as a bulwark against the imposition of right-wing populist agendas critics say run counter to the broader interests of local societies, but cater to the interests of certain domestic elites. It is within this context that we must consider the Brazilian election alongside other electoral processes in the democratic world.

content:
Lasten ja nuorten tekoälyn käyttö tapahtuu ennen kaikkea mobiililaitteilla. Tekoälyä käyttävistä peräti 94 prosenttia käyttää sitä puhelimellaan. Kyse ei ole satunnaisista kokeiluista, vaan lähes puolet tekoälyä käyttävistä lapsista ja nuorista hyödyntää sitä päivittäin.

title: HELDIG Summit 2026 Methodological encounters: Application deadline for talks and posters extended
content:
Dear reader,

We are gathering speakers and poster proposals for the next HELDIG Summit that aims to provide a snapshot of digital research in Social Sciences and Humanities today. To bring about discussion, we are planning three themes: digital history, digital social sciences and digital heritage. We invite you to contribute to this event with a 5-minute flash-talk or poster from recent or ongoing project(s). The Summit is a good opportunity to give visibility to your latest research and tools, get inspired by methodological innovations in similar fields, and make new connections.  

The HELDIG Summit brings together social sciences and humanities in a day that takes a snapshot at the state of the art in digital research. This year, we bring discussion around methodological and infrastructure encounters beyond disciplines. What challenges in data processing new methods enable us to overcome? How to maintain and adapt our research tools to fast-changing technological landscape? How to target the use of AI responsibly in the research cycle?  

The Summit will take place on December 4 (10:00-18:00), including a cocktail reception.

title: AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
content:
For much of the last month, many of the cybersecurity experts I talk to and follow have been posting like they are very scared. Many have been warning of an AI-powered “Black Swan” event, have been alarmed by the number of vulnerabilities suddenly discovered, and of the apparent power of AI agents and large language models more broadly to find and exploit previously unknown bugs. 

The rhetoric has ranged from worried-but-measured (things are about to get weird), to run-of-the-mill advice like update your software and make sure you have two-factor authentication on, to vagueposting about AI-powered attacks, to things like ‘the internet was nice while it lasted,’ to outright prepper-level terror.

title: Ukraine’s Medical Evacuations Go Airborne
content:
A recent video released by Ukraine’s 92nd Assault Brigade reportedly showed a heavy bomber drone helping to evacuate a soldier, in what was the world’s first attempt to use a drone for the mission. “Due to high enemy drone activity and mined terrain, evacuating him using traditional unmanned ground systems was impossible,” said the brigade.

The soldier, Kostiantyn Vlasenko, had been cut off for months and had lost a leg. In the end, alone and fearing gangrene, he decided to amputate the other. Earlier attempts to reach him had failed.

Ukraine has been testing medical evacuations with aerial drones throughout this year and had previously used ground robots.

“This is the first time in human history that such an operation has been carried out,” says Anatolii, a commander of a mortar battery unit from the unit. “I think we’ll see it happen more often, but everything will depend on the conditions . . . [it works best] in rain or fog.”

The widespread use of drones across the front, and the expansion of the kill zone, moving in and out and getting the wounded evacuated from the front has become a very dangerous job.

title: Mehdi Hasan on AIPAC's Role in El-Sayed vs. Rogers Race in Michigan & Trump's Targeting of Ilhan Omar
content:
One of the most closely watched races in the midterm elections is in Michigan between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. El-Sayed is a former public health official who is campaigning on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting corporate money out of politics. Rogers is a former Republican congressman backed by President Trump.

If elected, El-Sayed would become the first Muslim to serve in the U.S. Senate. During Wednesday’s debate in Michigan, Rogers repeated the claim, without providing evidence, that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied the accusation.

“If Abdul El-Sayed wins, it will be a reminder that the left can win in a swing state like Michigan,” says Mehdi Hasan, editor-in-chief of Zeteo. “And it will be actually a moment to say, 'You know what? Americans rejected Islamophobia.'”

title: VM antoi esityksen ammattidieselistä – Yrittäjiltä välitön älähdys
content:
Hallitus on antanut torstaina esityksen raskaan liikenteen ammattidieselistä, tiedottaa valtiovarainministeriö.

Esityksen mukaan ammattidieselin polttoaineveronpalautus olisi 3,3 senttiä litralta. Palautukseen olisivat oikeutettuja linja-autot ja kuorma-autot, joiden suurin sallittu paino kuormattuna on vähintään 7,5 tonnia.

PALAUTUSTA voisi esityksen mukaan hakea tammi-kesäkuun ja heinä-joulukuun ajalta tai koko kalenterivuodelta kerralla.

Veronpalautuksen olisi tarkoitus tulla voimaan, kun EU:n polttoaineen jakelun päästökauppa alkaa vuoden 2028 alussa. Verotuen on määrä olla voimassa vuoden 2037 loppuun saakka.

Ammattidieseliä ovat ajaneet muun muassa kuljetusala ja elinkeinoelämä.

SUOMEN yrittäjät (SY) arvostelee esitystä tuoreeltaan riittämättömäksi. Järjestö vaatii tiedotteessaan palautuksen tason nostamista ja ammattidieselin käyttöönoton aikaistamista.

– Hyvä, että ammattidiesel etenee, mutta 3,3 sentin palautus on liian pieni ja vuosi 2028 liian myöhään. Yritykset tarvitsevat helpotusta kustannuksiin nopeammin, SY:n johtava ekonomisti Petri Malinen sanoo.

title: Amplifying Women’s Voice: The SheSaid Campaign in the Igbo Community
content:
The Shesaid campaign is an international campaign under the umbrella of Wiki Loves Women that focuses on the creation and improvements of entries about Women on Wikiquote. This campaign amplifies Women Voice and addresses persistent gender gap in the representation of notable women across the digital space. This year the Igbo Wikimedians User Group joins the international campaign, to address gender gap in the representation of notable women across digital platforms like Wikiquote and Wikipedia.

From 2nd September to 30th September 2026, the Igbo Wikimedia community participated in the SheSaid campaign, an initiative aimed at amplifying women’s voices and improving their representation on Wikiquote. The campaign brought contributors together to document the words, ideas, and wisdom of notable women in the Igbo language.

The campaign was organized by Akwugo, Lucy Iwuala, Sylvaline39, Ebube Clara, and Vivian Amalachukwu, who worked together to encourage participation, provide training, and support contributors throughout the campaign.

title: What telecoms leave behind when they exit a country

When telecoms pull out of markets, data protection and human rights commitments often disappear

By Jie Zhang 

This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In March 2022, just over a year after Myanmar’s military coup, Telenor, the Norwegian telecommunications giant, sold its subsidiary in the country to M1 Group, bringing nearly eight years of operation to an end. title: Omid and Chamran Ahmadinejad Arrested by IRGC Intelligence Agents in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, Omid and Chamran Ahmadinejad, two residents of Ahvaz, were arrested.

Based on information obtained by HRANA, the two cousins were arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in the early hours of Wednesday, October 21, and transferred to one of the agency’s detention facilities in Ahvaz.

A source close to the families confirmed the arrests to HRANA, stating: “Chamran Ahmadinejad was arrested at his home. Omid Ahmadinejad, who worked at a foam manufacturing workshop owned by Chamran and also lived on the premises, was arrested at the workshop.”

The source added that agents simultaneously searched the men’s residences and confiscated several personal belongings, including a workplace computer, laptops, and mobile phones.

According to information received by HRANA, despite follow-up efforts by the families, the relevant authorities have yet to provide a clear explanation regarding the reasons for the arrests or the charges brought against the two men.

Chamran Ahmadinejad, 30, married, and his cousin Omid Ahmadinejad, 36, are originally from Bahmai County and reside in Ahvaz.

title: Uganda: Ensure Justice for Killing of Rwandan Dissident
content:
(Nairobi) – Ugandan authorities’ obligation to conduct an effective investigation into the brutal killing of a Rwandan dissident requires examining all evidence that points to a possible politically motivated killing, Human Rights Watch said today. Ugandan authorities should ensure a prompt, impartial, credible investigation that leads to accountability.

The body of Sgt. Maj. Robert Kabera, a singer, former Rwanda Defence Force member, and outspoken critic of the Rwandan government, was found on October 17, 2026, in Luwala village near Kampala, where he was constructing a house. He had fled Rwanda in November 2020 and claimed asylum on political persecution grounds. He had reported to Human Rights Watch multiple times that he had been threatened and attacked in Uganda. In a September 2022 interview with Human Rights Watch, Kabera said: “They will kill me. They know where I am … I will die before I get resettled.”

title: Sexual Assaults on Campus No Longer Scrutinized as Closely Under Trump’s Education Department
content:
The civil rights arm of the U.S. Department of Education has dramatically scaled back investigations involving schools and colleges since the second Trump administration began, even as complaints continue to pour in, a ProPublica analysis of newly obtained records found.

The analysis shows how severely the department’s Office for Civil Rights has retracted from its mission, launching an average of about 100 new investigations a month — 1,839 total from Inauguration Day in 2025 through July 2026. The OCR launched an average of 310 new investigations each month in 2024 during the Biden administration, according to data previously obtained by ProPublica.

Under President Donald Trump, the OCR abandoned the public-facing list of schools it was investigating and the reasons for those investigations, including claims of discrimination based on race, sex and disability. ProPublica sued the department to obtain internal case data. The government subsequently provided records of the OCR’s actions in the first 18 months of Trump’s return to power, and we are publishing the data so the public can search the cases.

title: How K-dramas use Africa as a backdrop to boost South Korea’s image
content:
The success of South Korean popular music or K-pop continues to power the Hallyu Wave, a term that describes the global obsession with the country’s pop culture production.

But before K-pop came the spread of K-drama, TV series from the country, starting in the late 1990s. By 2024 the melodrama Queen of Tears ranked as the most watched Korean series on Netflix, becoming the 14th most watched show of all time on the streaming service. It followed on the success of many other hits like Crash Landing on You and Marry My Husband.

K-drama has led to the development of another trend: Africa repeatedly appears as a homogeneous place full of savage danger or childish immaturity, and in need of a Korean saviour.

As a scholar of film and media, with a specific interest in global Black art and film practices, I recently studied how and why Africa became this trope in K-drama. This is particularly true in rags-to-riches romance stories and melodramas.

I traced Africa’s presence in three K-dramas – Shooting Stars (2022), Marry My Husband (2024) and Queen of Tears (2024). In them, Africa appears in three different negative ways:

  • in need of charity

    • in need of charity

  • a place of rebellion and savagery
snippet: The success of South Korean popular music or K-pop continues to power the Hallyu Wave, a term that describes the global obsession with the country’s pop culture production.
creator: Osarugue Otebele, Assistant Professor, Cinema Studies Institute, University of Toronto

title: Giving Amsterdam's streets a face
content: If you live in a European city, it's likely your street is named after someone. But do you know who that person was, what they did to earn a place on the map, or what they looked like? In Amsterdam, finding out might be a little easier. Many streets, squares, and bridges feature information panels with a portrait and a short biography of the historical figure they are named after. And all this thanks to a grassroots initiative run by two Amsterdam residents. Geef straten een gezicht (“Give streets a face”) is a project launched by photographer and graphic designer Paul Fennis in 2013. He installs portraits and short biographies to help people understand the history behind their street names. Since 2020, journalist and writer Shirley Brandeis has worked with him on the project. “It started as a one-off thing,” Brandeis told The European Correspondent. Fennis lived on a square named after J. J. Cremer, a Dutch writer who campaigned against child labour. He often saw children from a nearby school playing there and thought they should know about him. title: AI Is Already 'Amplifying the Destruction' of War
content:
The UN met this week to discuss, among other things, the threat of autonomous weapons.

“The technology is developing at a pace that is very concerning,” Laurent Gisel, the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross’s (ICRC) legal warfare team, told 404 Media. Gisel was in NYC this week to address the UN about all the things that are driving conflict across the planet. His prepared remarks include a statement on the illegal arms trade, nuclear weapons, mines, and – of course – AI.

Autonomous weapons have been a hot topic at the UN this year. In September, the UN attempted to pass a treaty that would govern the use of killer AI weapons. Diplomats from Russia and the US stripped it of its power. 

But the UN has pressed forward. On Tuesday, the international governing body announced a new initiative that would grapple with the issue. But, as Gisel said: “multilateral processes take quite some time” and  “we already see the effects on the battlefield.” 

AI is already picking targets and killing people. Gisel said the technology is “amplifying the destruction, amplifying the violation of the law, amplifying the humanitarian harm caused by conflicts.”
snippet: The UN met this week to discuss, among other things, the threat of autonomous weapons.

title: Yemen: Huthis must open Ta’iz roads immediately as thousands of civilians’ lives are at risk
content:
The Huthi de facto authorities must immediately open vital roads in and around Ta’iz city, as fighting intensifies between the Huthis and government forces and moves closer to densely populated areas of the city, Amnesty International said today.  

The Huthis have tightened their control around Ta’iz city after they cut off the main road connecting Ta’iz to Aden in October, pushing the city to the brink of a severe humanitarian disaster. They have blocked humanitarian aid, putting access to food, water, and healthcare for hundreds of thousands at grave risk as per UN agencies. 

“The residents of Ta’iz, Yemen’s third largest city, have endured years of hardship due to the conflict, while hosting the country’s largest number of internally displaced people. At various points since 2015, Huthi forces have surrounded the city, blocking access to major roads connecting it  to other towns and cities and forcing civilians to use dangerous and poorly maintained mountained roads,” said Heba Morayef, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for Middle East and North Africa.

title: A Silicon Curtain Is Descending Across the Semiconductor World
content:
The annual ISSCC Forum is dubbed the “Olympics of Chips.”  As a young engineer, I attended. Despite intense commercial competition, the global forum wowed me. The brightest minds from MIT, Stanford, Cambridge, and elsewhere competed with engineers from major chip firms for attention to their breakthroughs in solid-state circuits and systems-on-a-chip. 

This year’s forum in San Francisco featured MediaTek’s Rick Tsai from Taiwan, IBM’s Heike Riel, Cadence’s Anirudh Devgan, and Apple’s Hope Giles. But the public program listed no plenary speaker from a major Chinese chip or AI company.

Global technical exchange and commercial networking built the chip industry. Engineers, chipmakers, equipment suppliers, customers, and investors met at the same conferences and trade shows. That cooperative international circuit is now broken into a world of rival technology industries, with democratic semiconductor powers pitted against authoritarian China.

title: From Incubator to a Living Language: Ten Years of Tulu Wikipedia
content:
For a language community, a Wikipedia can be more than an encyclopedia. It can become a meeting place, a digital archive, a learning space, and a way of making a language visible on the internet. The ten-year journey of Tulu Wikipedia illustrates how a small volunteer community can gradually build a digital ecosystem for a language. or Tulu, this journey has been especially significant. Before Tulu Wikipedia became a full Wikimedia project in 2016, Tulu had only a limited presence in the digital world. Despite being spoken by a large community along the southwest coast of India called Tulunadu, the language had relatively little freely accessible digital content and few online resources through which people could learn, document and share knowledge in Tulu.

The challenge was particularly important for a language recognised by UNESCO as endangered. Digital presence can play an important role in the long-term visibility and transmission of such languages, especially as younger generations increasingly encounter knowledge through the internet.

title: Europe gave us the freedom to move – without the right to stay
content:
Housing goes beyond building houses. It shapes where and how we live, work, raise our children, grow old – and which territories thrive or will be abandoned. It is about people. It is about dignity and trust. Housing is about hope: the promise that wherever you live, whoever you are, you are welcome in Europe and have a right to stay. 

Decades. Billions. This is what it took to build one of the EU’s greatest achievements: the freedom to move. But what freedom is this, when staying is no longer possible? What freedom when forced to move? A right to stay starts with a place to stay. One you call home. Someplace you can own, rent or simply afford. A place to build a life. That is why it is more than simply building houses. Housing is about life.

title: Mali: Army, Russia’s ‘Africa Corps’ Commit New Abuses
content:
(Nairobi) – Mali’s armed forces and the allied Russia-controlled Africa Corps have committed new atrocities against civilians in central Mali during renewed fighting, Human Rights Watch said today. 

On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others. Between May and August, Malian and Africa Corps forces held numerous detainees inhumanely in a metal container at an army base in Sévaré town, Mopti region, where many were tortured, including with severe beatings, electric shock, and waterboarding. 

“Civilians are bearing the brunt of the Mali junta’s failure to rein in its abusive forces and allies,” said Ilaria Allegrozzi, senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Recent atrocities implicate the Malian army as well as Russia-controlled Africa Corps, for which Russian officials should also be held accountable.”

title: Kekrikarnevaalit Kärpäsen kirjastossa 29.10. – Halloween-viikon ohjelmassa myös taskulamppuseikkailua pääkirjastossa

Kummitukset valtaavat Kärpäsen kirjaston ja edellisenä päivänä pääkirjaston lasten alueella seikkaillaan taskulampun valossa.


Lahden kirjastoissa on Halloweenin aikaan lapsiperheille jännittäviä ja elämyksellisiä tapahtumia. Kaikista Lahden kirjastoista löytyy myös Halloween teemaista luettavaa. Lisäksi kirjaston somekanavista löydät myös halloweentunnelmaa henkiviä lastenkirjavinkkejä.


Kärpäsen kekrikarnevaaleissa tämän- ja tuonpuoleisen raja on seitinohut… On kummitusten vuoro käydä kirjastossa.

Tapahtumassa saat vinkkejä, miten toimia aaveiden ja muiden kirjaston vallanneiden myyttisten olentojen kanssa. Sulaudu joukkoon pukeutumalla teeman mukaisesti etukäteen, tai askartele oma naamio kirjastossa. Pääset myös karkottamaan kirjastosta pahoja henkiä.

Klo 18 kokoonnutaan monitoimitilaan Kupariketun kekritarina -esitystä varten. Kuparikettu on modernin kansanperinteen asiantuntija, joka johdattaa kuulijat mystiseen kekriseikkailuun.

title: From Flights to ‘Incentives,’ Indonesian Nickel Giant Harita Approved Payments for Local Politicians and Leaders
content:
When senior mining executive Stevi Thomas was convicted alongside an Indonesian governor for bribery in 2024, the ruling was seen as a rare case of accountability for corruption in the Southeast Asian nation. 

The court case revealed how the politician had received some $60,000 in bribes for facilitating permits for Harita Group, a conglomerate that has sourced up to eight percent of the world’s nickel supply in recent years  — and has also left a trail of environmental damage in its wake. 

Now, leaked internal records obtained by OCCRP reveal a host of other payments that Harita executives earmarked for local politicians, individuals identified by the firm as community leaders, and the military between 2013 and 2023. 

The planned or approved payments amounted to at least $389,000 and took the form of flights for politicians, “incentives” for the community leaders, and financial support for military projects. 

Evidence of these outlays was found in leaked company emails, internal memos, and invoices.

Reporters were unable to independently verify if the money was ultimately disbursed in every instance, or establish the precise purpose of some of the approved payments.

title: America’s death penalty: why executions are rising again
content:
After two decades of decline, the number of executions in the United States began rising sharply again in 2025. Last year, 47 people were put to death – the highest number in more than 15 years. So far in 2026, another 31 people have been executed.

The resurgence comes amid renewed controversy over capital punishment, following the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee and a proposal to livestream a military execution, which President Donald Trump subsequently walked back.

But according to Carolyn Strange, emeritus professor of history at the Australian National University, these controversies have striking precedents in American history.

Pike is not the first person to survive an execution attempt. In 1946, Willie Francis survived the electric chair in Louisiana. After an unsuccessful legal challenge, the state executed him in 1947.

Strange says the history of capital punishment in the US is marked by repeated attempts to make executions more humane – or at least appear that way. From the electric chair to lethal injections, new methods were introduced with the promise of making death quicker and more efficient.

title: Albania’s future: from a mixed system to an EU member?
content:
In October 2026, several government buildings were set on fire in Tirana, Albania. For months, young Albanians had protested Jared Kushner’s planned multi-billion luxury resort on the island of Sazan and the nearby Vjosa-Narta coastal area. What began as an environmentalist and anti-corruption movement soon sprung into a wide unrest against the government and Albanian officials’ lack of transparency in public procurement and in general – The Flamingo Revolution, named after the birds living on Sazan, whose pictures the dissatisfied citizens have carried on their protest signs. 

Freedom of assembly is at the core of rule of law, as is transparency in public procurement and decision-making. Yet, there has been wide violence between police and the protesters, especially in the last two weeks. Prime minister Edi Rama, whose government aims for European Union membership by 2030, has claimed the protests are fuelled by disinformation and foreign interference. One of the protesters’ main aims is Rama’s resignation.

title: Playing by the rules?
content: The strength of courts, rights and checks on power is declining across Europe, reflecting a broader global recession, according to data from the World Justice Project’s Rule of Law Index. The index measures eight factors, including checks on government power, the absence of corruption and the justice system. Since 2021, Europe's average score has fallen in seven of the eight areas, and remained unchanged in one: corruption. Although the declines are small, less than 1.5 points out of 100, they are consistent. Two-thirds of European countries scored lower in 2026 than in 2021. Russia, Belarus, Türkiye and Serbia remain at the bottom of the European rankings, but some of the steepest declines were also recorded in Georgia, Portugal and Slovakia. Europe still scores substantially higher than the global average, and nine of the world's ten highest-ranked countries are European.

title: Kenyan youth activist Erica Njuguna: “Gen Z are uniquely impacted by climate crisis”
content:
Erica Njuguna is a 22-year-old Kenyan youth climate justice activist, who is fighting for a fossil-free, debt-free and just future. She is the global coordinator for ANGRY (The Alliance of Non-governmental Radical Youth) and started her climate activism in 2017 after a severe drought led to water rationing across Kenya, including in Nairobi.

Here, Erica talks to Amnesty International about joining the Fridays for Future movement, what it’s like to take to take to the streets in protest and why climate reparations are vital.

I became a climate justice organizer after I experienced firsthand the impacts of the climate crisis. In 2017, there was a huge drought that led to a lot of water shortages and water rationing, including in Nairobi. Life was unliveable at the time.

I joined the Fridays for Future Movement when I was still in high school.

title: From Curiosity to Contribution: My Journey with WikiSeloka
content:
I was introduced to WikiSeloka by my friend Elicefa, who is actively involved in the project of WikiSeloka. At first, I was not familiar with WikiSeloka or its activities. After learning more about it, I discovered that WikiSeloka is a collaborative initiative that aims to preserve cultural heritage by documenting and digitizing oral literature.

As someone with a strong interest in linguistics and language studies, I saw WikiSeloka as a great opportunity to learn new things. I am particularly interested in the diversity of regional languages in Indonesia, many of which reflect the rich history, values, and traditions of their communities. This interest encouraged me to join WikiSeloka, attend its weekly meetings, and take part in the project. For me, it was a chance to expand my knowledge of languages and learn how digital technology can help preserve regional languages.

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of one of the prisoners executed at dawn today, Wednesday, October 21, as Ahmad (last name unknown). The identity of the second prisoner remains under investigation.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the two prisoners had previously been arrested on murder charges in separate cases and subsequently sentenced to death by criminal courts.

At the time of this report, the executions of these two prisoners had not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
snippet: According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

title: Collapsed Surrogacy Agency Loses U.S. Civil Case After Court No-Show
content:
Collapsed international surrogacy agency World Center of Baby has been dealt a double blow in Florida, with a judge ruling against its U.S. corporate entity in a civil lawsuit – shortly after another case against the company was filed.

The developments come just over a month after OCCRP published a global investigation into the chaos World Center of Baby left in its wake after announcing it was filing for bankruptcy, including surrogates left unpaid and unsupported, and prospective parents abandoned. 

In a decision made publicly available on Tuesday, Judge Thomas Ramsberger in Florida’s Sixth Circuit Court ruled in favor of a U.K.-based couple who brought a case against the agency’s U.S. corporate entity World Center Group Corp and two of its representatives. The complaint was on five counts, including breach of contract and fraud. 

The lawsuit accused the company of “a calculated and coordinated scheme” to secure substantial payments for promised services despite its worsening financial and operational problems.

title: Youth protests across Europe: the overlapping crises facing Gen Z
content:
Young people are facing a future that feels increasingly uncertain. Although every generation experiences turbulence while navigating adolescence, the pressures experienced by Gen Z – those born between 1997 and 2012 – are different and seem more pervasive.

From climate change and mental health concerns to academic pressure, housing costs, job and economic insecurity, today’s young people are navigating a complex set of expectations. Understanding their frustrations, including those expressed through protests across Europe, requires looking beyond individual experiences to the social conditions shaping their lives.

Adolescence has long been seen as a period of “storm and stress”. This reflecting a belief that is a universal and inevitable period of emotional turmoil, behavioural conflict and identity crisis. However, this has been increasingly challenged.

Rather than being defined solely by difficulty and disruption, adolescence is increasingly viewed as a period of possibility, opportunity and growth. Yet realising that potential depends heavily on the social environments in which young people grow up.

title: Cops Warned to Look for ‘Suspicious Behavior’ From People Opposing Flock at City Council Meetings
content:
A federal intelligence center warned police that city council meetings about Flock “may be viewed by extremists as a desirable target,” and told them to be on the lookout for “emotional confrontations” between people who oppose surveillance and government officials, according to a copy of the warning obtained by 404 Media.

The warning, obtained by 404 Media, was issued by the Orange County Intelligence Assessment Center (OCIAC)—a government fusion center—in July to police in California. 404 Media recently obtained the bulletin using a Freedom of Information Act request.

This surveillance bulletin to cops is the latest evidence that police around the country have been told to be on edge during public meetings where people are participating in democracy and utilizing their First Amendment rights about unpopular things the government is doing. We have reported on a spate of people being illegally arrested for extremely minor procedural violations or for cursing at city council meetings about Flock and data centers while participating in constitutionally protected activities.

title: Openness in AI development: a path to long-term independence
content:
As concerns grow over deepening dependencies on a handful of Big Tech companies and the outsized influence of the U.S. and China, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk used his speech during July’s inaugural Global Dialogue on AI Governance to call on humans to “take back our agency” over AI. But what does agency over AI really mean? What policies and practices can allow people to shape AI in ways that respect, rather than undermine, human rights? 

This blog post unpacks concrete initiatives that show how openness in AI development can increase people’s agency over AI and advance the development of public interest technology. At the same time, we reflect on how openness is not the same thing as mere access, and how short-term pragmatism can pave the way toward long-term independence.

title: Sri Lanka: New counterterrorism bill risks perpetuating past abuses
content:
The Sri Lankan government’s proposed new counterterrorism legislation allows wide scope for abuse and poses serious threats to human rights, said Amnesty International in a new legal analysis.

Despite some improvements on the previous white paper of the law issued in late 2025, the Protection of the State from Terrorism bill, which will replace the repressive and long-standing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), retains an overly broad and ambiguous definition of terrorism that leaves room for arbitrary interpretation and the potential criminalization of dissent, protest, and the activities of civil society organizations.

The bill, which was tabled on 6 October, is now before the Supreme Court to check its compatibility with Sri Lanka’s Constitution. Depending on the Supreme Court’s determination, the law is set to be debated by Sri Lanka’s parliament in the coming weeks.

title: Revealed: Expensive gas behind ‘nearly 90%’ of rise in UK electricity bills
content:
A surge in wholesale costs driven by expensive gas is responsible for nearly 90% of the rise in UK household electricity bills since 2020, reveals new analysis.

The figures, shared with Carbon Brief by thinktank Nesta, show that wholesale gas costs are also behind the vast majority (77%) of the increase in household gas bills.

The analysis firmly contradicts the idea, which has become embedded in UK media and political narratives, that the UK’s net-zero target is to blame for high energy bills.

Andrew Sissons, director for sustainable future at Nesta, tells Carbon Brief that net-zero is, in fact, “helping to shelter Britain from the impact of expensive gas”. He adds: 

“Rising gas prices, not net-zero, have driven most of the recent surge in Britain’s energy bills. Britain is particularly exposed, with over 80% of households connected to gas mains, while our electricity system still relies too much on gas as the marginal unit.”

The analysis comes after the UK government gave its approval for the Jackdaw gas field to be developed in the North Sea, despite stating that it “would not…affect prices”.

title: Pen Pushers Help Engineers Keep Ukraine’s Lights On
content:
Russia’s campaign against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure is forcing the country to rethink a system built around large power plants and long transmission lines. The answer is increasingly decentralized generation: smaller gas-fired units, cogeneration, batteries, modular boiler houses, renewables, and backup systems closer to consumers.

Kyiv has been expanding smaller, distributed sources of electricity and heat, alongside storage and backup generation, to make energy supply less vulnerable to Russian strikes. But it still depends on local implementation.

The decisive question will be if Ukraine’s municipalities have the institutional capacity to turn money, equipment, and plans into functioning systems.

In March, comprehensive resilience plans for regions and regional centers were approved. They focused on protection of critical infrastructure, development of distributed generation, backup and alternative power, and decentralization of heat generation. Kyiv said these were long-term measures to strengthen communities beyond a single winter.

title: Release Dr Hussam Abu Safiya and 13 other doctors held without charge
content:
CIVICUS and Physicians for Human Rights – Israel add Dr Abu Safiya to the Stand As My Witness campaign, calling for the release of all 14 detained Gaza doctors. 

Johannesburg, 21 October 2026 – Dr Hussam Abu Safiya treated children in northern Gaza until Israeli forces took him from his hospital. Almost two years on, he is still held in inhumane conditions without charge or trial, and he is not alone. 

Dr Abu Safiya, a paediatrician and director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, stayed with his patients through attacks, evacuation orders, and severe medicine shortages. He was detained on 27 December 2024 and has since been held under Israel’s Unlawful Combatants Law, much of the time in solitary confinement and without adequate healthcare.  

Physicians for Human Rights – Israel (PHRI) and his lawyer report repeated severe assaults and a serious decline in his health. In June 2026, Israel’s Supreme Court upheld his detention until at least October.

title: The WhatsApp bot that signed up 1,000 people for Palestine in 48 hours
content:
On the night of 1 October 2025, the Israeli navy stopped the boats of the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters, on their way to Gaza. Many of them had sailed from Barcelona a month earlier, and the people detained included the city’s former mayor, Ada Colau. Within hours there were hundreds of people outside the Israeli consulate on Avinguda Carles III, and the flotilla’s organizers were calling for protests the next evening in every town in Catalonia.

If you were in Catalonia that week and wanted to show up, the hard part was finding out where. The information was spread across Instagram stories, Telegram channels and family group chats, and half of it was out of date by the time it reached you. One WhatsApp number tried to fix that. You wrote to it and it told you what was happening with the boats and where the nearest protest was.

The bot was called Solidaritat amb Palestina (Solidarity with Palestine). It was built by the Barcelona collective procom.dev and it told people in Catalonia what was happening and where to go. It passed 1,000 users in two days, and 80% of them arrived through a forwarded link.

title: Osa CSC:n palveluista pois käytöstä varotoimena PHP-haavoittuvuuden takia
content:
Korjattu ohjelmistoversio otetaan käyttöön mahdollisimman pian sen julkaisun jälkeen kaikissa ympäristöissä, joissa PHP on käytössä.

Varotoimena olemme ajaneet alas osan palveluistamme. Tämän toimenpiteen tarkoitus on varotoimenpiteenä suojata palveluja kunnes korjauspäivitykset on tehty. Käyttökatko ei siis johdu siitä, että tiedossamme olisi tapauksia, joissa haavoittuvuutta olisi käytetty hyväksi.

Viestimme palvelukohtaisesti pois käytöstä otettujen palveluiden vastuutahoille.

PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) on yksi maailman suosituimmista palvelimiin liittyvistä ohjelmointikielistä ja sitä hyödyntää iso osa internetin verkkosivustoista. Teemme päivitykset välittömästi niiden julkaisun jälkeen ja pyrimme palauttamaan palvelut normaalitilaan mahdollisimman nopeasti.

content:
“If this report amounts to one finding above all the others, it is this: recognition was never the finish line, only the starting condition. Culture’s value has rarely been stated this clearly or this often by European institutions and, yet, it still has not been matched by the funding, protection, or governance necessary for it to be realised. Two years ago, the question this report asked was whether culture could be heard at all. This edition asks a harder one: now that it has been, what is it actually allowed to do with that recognition?”
— Lars Ebert, State of Culture 2026

The central contradiction running through State of Culture 2026 is that culture is praised more than ever and protected less than ever. It is a public good in every EU institution’s vocabulary, yet still funded and evaluated as though it were an industrial output, measured in projects, KPIs and short cycles.

title: "When the Bubble Bursts": Naomi Klein & Astra Taylor on Reclaiming Democracy from AI Oligarchs
content:
We’re joined by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor, co-authors of the book End Times Fascism, for a wide-ranging conversation on the multitrillion-dollar global investment in artificial intelligence and its reverberating effects around the world.

Klein recently spoke at the People’s AI Assembly, alongside other critics of the artificial intelligence industry, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former chair of the Federal Trade Commission Lina Khan. “The resistance to AI is taking many forms, and it’s really a resistance to oligarch power, which is concentrated in the hands of these tech companies,” Klein tells Democracy Now! “After 50 years of outsourcing and hollowing out of public functions of the state, the very last stage is the outsourcing of thinking, of intelligence itself.”

title: Perussuomalaiset lupaa leikkauslistaansa torstaille
content:
Perussuomalaiset aikoo julkaista torstaina ehdotuksensa sopeutuskeinoista ensi vaalikaudelle. Puolue lupaa, että tarjolla on lähinnä saksimista, ei veronkiristyksiä.

Puolueen puheenjohtaja, valtiovarainministeri Riikka Purra kertoi esitysaikataulusta keskiviikkona eduskunnassa toimittajille.

Hänen mukaansa sopeutuslista painottuu voimakkaasti menoleikkauksiin.

Puolue ei esitä työhön eikä yrittämiseen veronkiristyksiä.

MIKÄÄN AIHEALUE ei Purran mukaan ole suojassa leikkauksilta.

Puolue aikoo esittää säästöjä etenkin maahanmuuton kuluihin.

Eläkkeitäkään ei voida sulkea sopeutusten ulkopuolelle, mutta Purra ei vielä avannut tarkemmin puolueen ehdotusta.

Kokonaisuus on puheenjohtajan mukaan vaaditun kokoinen, hieman isompikin.

PUOLUEIDEN säästölistojen taustalla on parlamentaarinen velkajarrusopimus, jonka mukaan julkista taloutta tulee sopeuttaa ensi vaalikaudella 8-11 miljardia euroa tämänhetkisen arvion mukaan.

Kokoomus julkaisi oman, yhdeksän miljardin suuruisen sopeutusehdotuksensa syyskuun lopussa.

title: Impact of PHP vulnerabilities on Wikimedia Cloud Services
content:
On October 20, 2026, we took Wikimedia Cloud Services (WMCS) and other services offline as a precaution due to two significant vulnerabilities that were discovered in PHP, the programming language most of our services rely on. The PHP Foundation published an advisory ahead of the announcement due to the significance of these vulnerabilities. 

Keeping the Wikimedia projects and their users secure and safe is our top priority. A significant amount of information on the Wikimedia projects is public and available for everyone, but our projects necessarily contain some personal information that is critical to keep private. Protecting user privacy is an essential part of free knowledge, and the Wikimedia Foundation Privacy Policy commits us to strive to keep non-public personal information secure.

title: Introducing Our New Surveillance Self-Defense Guide: Online Privacy for Parents and Youth
content:
The internet is a vast and confusing place no matter your age. Trying to help youth engage with it safely and privately is a complicated topic that touches on many different skillsets and ideas. But just because it’s complicated doesn’t mean it’s impossible. We’ve launched our Online Privacy for Parents and Youth Surveillance Self-Defense guide in hopes to provide a framework for finding solutions that work for you. 

EFF rolls out this crucial resource as state and local governments consider ill-advised laws that cut young people off from essential information and experiences. This particularly harms vulnerable youth and marginalized groups who often find safety in supportive online communities they can't access offline. Such laws also entail age gating, which compromises the privacy of all internet users and stifles young users’ ability to learn, grow, and express themselves.

title: Norway’s EUSBSR accession opens new opportunities for cooperation in education and social inclusion
content:

For Policy Area Education, the occasion was also an opportunity to strengthen dialogue with Norwegian stakeholders and explore new possibilities for cooperation on shared societal challenges.

Norway became the ninth participating country in the EUSBSR on 18 May 2026, marking an important step in strengthening cooperation across the Baltic Sea Region.

The official launch event in Oslo on 16 October brought together Norwegian Minister of Foreign Affairs Espen Barth Eide, Minister of Local Government and Regional Development Bjørnar Skjæran, representatives of the European Commission, Policy Area Coordinators and stakeholders from across the region.

The programme focused on Norway’s role in the Strategy, its longstanding experience of Baltic Sea cooperation and the opportunities that full participation creates for contributing to shared priorities.

title: Protest as a pillar of democracy
content:
Protest helps close the gap between the promise of democracy and the formal structures we actually have

Originally published on Global Voices

Image via Canva Pro.

This piece is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Democracy is often presented as an orderly, structured system of representation and deliberation, colorless and linear like an organizational version of the faux-classical architecture so many democratic countries adopt for their government buildings. Voting leads to representatives, debates lead to votes on laws, participation leads to action, like columns leading to a pediment.

title: January 2026 Protests: Ilya Ben-Rashid Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Ilya Ben-Rashid, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests and currently held in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan, has been sentenced to death, imprisonment, and additional punishments.

The verdict was issued by Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court and communicated to Ben-Rashid yesterday. Under the ruling, he was sentenced to death on the charge of moharebeh (waging war against God) through participation in the destruction of public property.

The same court also sentenced him to three years, six months, and one day of discretionary imprisonment on the charge of assembly and collusion to commit crimes against national security, and nine months and one day in prison on the charge of propaganda against the regime, with time already served in detention credited toward his sentence.

Additionally, as a supplementary punishment, he was sentenced to a two-year travel ban prohibiting him from leaving the country.

In April of this year, a hearing on the charges against Ben-Rashid was held before the same branch of the court.

title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty
content:
Burkina Faso’s unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code that restores the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and importation of expired or prohibited products. The country had abolished the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 2018 while its last known judicial execution took place in 1988.

Reinstating capital punishment sends a chilling message to critics of the military junta and risks becoming another tool to suppress dissent. Since the September 2022 military coup, Burkina Faso’s junta has steadily dismantled civic and political rights. Authorities have banned media outlets, suspended unions and civil society organizations, abolished multiparty politics, and subjected critics to arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances, unlawful conscription, and torture.

Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala defended the decision to reinstate the death penalty as a necessary measure to combat terrorism. He said that armed groups exploited the previous law’s leniency by promising new recruits they would face no more than life imprisonment if convicted of terrorist acts.

title: Why Doesn’t the US Implement Its Treaties?
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 21 October 2026 (IDN) – The US Senate—usually the Republican members—rejects multilateral treaties as if it were a sport. Others it rejects through inaction—the Law of the Sea Treaty, for example, negotiated under President Jimmy Carter and fruitlessly pushed for ratification by every president since. Republicans justify their blocking tactics by arguing that such treaties threaten sovereignty.

However, after almighty struggles—it takes only one third of the Senate to block a treaty—the important nuclear arms treaties with the Soviet Union and Russia were ratified. So was the Convention against Torture, which Republican President Ronald Reagan successfully fought for but which President George Bush junior illegally ignored, without a word of protest from Congress or most of the media. His vice-president, Dick Cheney, became torturer-in-chief and should have been arrested by the incoming Obama Administration. But Obama, wanting a peaceful life with Congress for the sake of future legislation, decided not to prosecute the torturers.

In October 2013, Syria joined the Chemical Weapons Treaty that the US has long been a party to.

title: IJ4EU award winner puts prize money towards new journalism fellowship
content:
IJ4EU grantee Investigate Europe is using its €5,000 IJ4EU Impact Award prize to fund a new fellowship offering aspiring journalists from under-represented backgrounds paid experience in cross-border reporting.

The journalism cooperative has teamed up with the Centre for Investigative Journalism (CIJ) to establish the CIJ Investigate Europe Lyra McKee Fellowship. It will offer one or two part-time paid placements working alongside Investigate Europe’s reporters, according to a CIJ announcement.

Investigate Europe and its partners won a 2025 IJ4EU Impact Award for Deadly Prices, an investigation into unequal access to medicines across Europe. The series examined how opaque pricing arrangements and pharmaceutical industry practices put essential treatments beyond patients’ reach.

The fellowship is open exclusively to graduates of the CIJ’s Lyra McKee bursary scheme, which provides five months of training and mentoring to people seeking to enter journalism or taking their first steps in the profession.

title: Runo nostaa metelin ja perhesuhteissa kuohuu
content:
Lahden kaupunginteatterin kevään 2027 uutuuksissa runo synnyttää poliittisen kohun ja läheiset perhesuhteet joutuvat koetukselle. Ohjelmistossa nähdään kaksi kantaesitystä ja yksi suomenkielinen kantaesitys.

Ennen sosiaalista mediaa meillä oli Huuto. Vuonna 1969 Yleisradion radioteatteri esitti yhdysvaltalaisen beat-runoilijan Allen Ginsbergin kulttirunon Huudon. Kansanedustaja Arne Berner teki ohjelmasta eduskuntakyselyn, jonka allekirjoitti 83 kansanedustajaa eri puolueista. Runon ympärille kasvoi valtakunnallinen kiista, josta eduskunta keskusteli vaalikeväänä kiivaasti neljä tuntia.

Lauri Maijalan käsikirjoittama ja ohjaama Huuto ja meteli saa kantaesityksensä 30.1.2027 Suurella näyttämöllä. Teos perustuu Yleisradion radioteatterin silloisen johtajan Pekka Lounelan ja dramaturgi Jyrki Mäntylän samannimiseen kirjaan sekä aikakauden lehtijuttuihin, uutisiin ja eduskunnan pöytäkirjoihin.

Maijalan käsissä Suuri näyttämö muuntautuu hämyiseksi 1960-luvun jazzklubiksi. Yhdentoista näyttelijän voimin esitys yhdistää fiktiolla terästetyn draaman ja elävän jazzmusiikin, kun yhden runon ympärille syntynyt kohu paisuu hallitsemattomaksi meteliksi. Samalla se vie katsojan keskelle kiistaa taiteen, sananvapauden ja julkisen keskustelun rajoista.

title: Museoiden taidekokoelmien verkkojulkaiseminen tarvitsee korvausmallin
content:
Museoiden digitaaliset taidekokoelmat tavoittavat uusia yleisöjä, mutta monella museolla ei ole varaa maksaa taiteilijoille teosten digikäytöstä. Kuvasto esittää lausunnossaan vuodelle 2027 valtion talousarvioon 1,5 miljoonan euron lisäystä, jolla laajennettaisiin taidekokoelmien saatavuutta verkossa ja turvataan taiteilijoiden korvaukset.

Museoiden digitaaliset taidekokoelmat ovat parantaneet taiteen saavutettavuutta. Kansalaiset ovat voineet tutustua vapaasti saatavilla oleviin teoksiin esimerkiksi Finna.fi-palvelussa. Samalla taideteosten tekijät ovat saaneet vuosittain tekijänoikeuskorvauksen teostensa verkkojulkaisemisesta. Valtio on investoinut merkittävästi taideteosten digitointiin.

Kuvasto ja Suomen museoliitto sopivat taidekokoelmien verkkojulkaisemisesta ja taiteilijoiden tekijänoikeuskorvauksista vuosina 2017–2024 voimassa olleessa sopimuksessa. Sen piirissä oli parhaimmillaan 45 museota ja säätiötä. Vuodesta 2025 alkaen museot ja säätiöt ovat voineet jatkaa teosten esittämistä verkossa Kuvaston Taidekokoelmat verkkoon 2.0 -sopimuksella. Sen on solminut yhteensä 29 museota ja säätiötä.

title: Vallan maantiede: Mikä on pelissä, kun Etiopia ja Eritrea etenevät kohti uutta sotaa?
content:
Lähes päivälleen seitsemän vuotta siitä, kun Etiopian pääministeri Abiy Ahmed sai Nobelin rauhanpalkinnon lopetettuaan sodan Eritrean kanssa, hän on matkalla kohti uutta sotaa pohjoista naapuriaan vastaan.

Maiden välinen konflikti uhkaa levitä laajemmaksi sodaksi alueella, jonka geopoliittinen painoarvo on noussut tulikuumaksi tänä vuonna.

Egypti, Somalia ja Eritrea ovat jo ehtineet muodostaa uuden liittouman Etiopiaa vastaan paperilla.

Kaiken keskiössä on Etiopian halu päästä käsiksi Punaiseenmereen. Siellä taistelevat nyt myös Jemenin huthit, jotka hiljattain liittyivät toden teolla mukaan Iranin puolelle Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin sodassa maata vastaan.

Monen maan intressit kiteytyvät pieneen merikaistaleeseen, ja sota Eritrean ja Eitopian välillä uhkaa koko aluetta.

Mitä tekevät Persianlahden maat, kun taistelu Punaisen meren kontrollista uhkaa eskaloitua entisestään?

title: Satokausi on pulkassa, vuodenkierto vaihtumassa uuteen – aika juhlia kekriä!
content:
Ympäri maailmaa löytyy juhlia sadonkorjuulle, vainajien muistamiselle ja vuoden vaihtumiselle. Kotoisen kekrimme sukulaisiin kuuluvat esimerkiksi kelttien Samhain, katolilaisen pyhäinpäivän ja Samhainin yhdistelmänä Yhdysvalloissa syntynyt Halloween ja meksikolaisten Kuolleiden päivä.

Kekrin juuret ulottuvat satojen vuosien päähän maataloudellisen satovuoden taitoskohtaan ajoittuvaan juhlintaan. Kekrin viettämisen ajankohta on vaihdellut syyskesästä myöhäissyksyyn sen mukaan, miten missäkin talossa on saatu kasvukauden työt valmiiksi.

1800-luvulla yhteiskunnan kehittymisen myötä kekrin viettämisen ajankohtaa täsmennettiin, ja se ajoitettiin pyhäinmiesten päivän yhteyteen marraskuun alkuun. Vuodesta 1955 pyhäinpäivä eli kekri on ollut nykyisellä paikallaan marraskuun ensimmäisenä lauantaina. Alun perin kekriin liittyneiden perinteiden, tapojen ja leikkien piirteitä löytyy nykyisin joulun ja uudenvuoden ajan vietosta.

title: Ulkoministeri Valtonen vierailee Sveitsissä
content:
Ulkoministeri Valtonen matkustaa Zürichiin ja Berniin 21.–22.10. ja tapaa ulkoministeri Ignazio Cassisin.

Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen ja Sveitsin ulkoministeri Ignazio Cassis keskustelevat ajankohtaisista ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan teemoista, Venäjän hyökkäyssodasta Ukrainaan ja Ukrainan ja tukemisesta sekä uusista teknologioista. ”Suomen ja Sveitsin diplomaattisuhteet täyttävät tänä vuonna 100 vuotta. Sveitsi ja Suomi kuuluvat maailman johtaviin innovaatiomaihin. Korkea innovaatiotiheys ja vahvat osaamiskeskittymät luovat erinomaiset edellytykset maidemme väliselle yhteistyölle. Meitä yhdistää myös halu vahvistaa monenkeskistä järjestelmää, myös uusien teknologioiden alalla”, Valtonen sanoo.

title: In a Vienna Bakery, Fresh Pastries and a Backdoor for Serbian Votes
content:
For the ordinary Viennese, it’s just another neighborhood Balkan bakery.

But to the more than 76,000 Serbians living in the Austrian capital, the shop known as Pekarica — "little bakery" — offers a fragrant touch of home, where orders are exchanged effortlessly in their native tongue as the scent of dough wafts from the oven.

That’s not all. On one recent morning, a customer stepped to the front of the counter, ignoring the steaming trays of braided breads and glossy pretzels entirely.

“Excuse me,” he said. “I was told by my colleagues that I can register to vote here.”

“Yes, you can,” the clerk replied, unfazed by the question. “Not here exactly, but further down. Come, I’ll take you.”

She led him out the door and a few steps down the pavement to the modest storefront housing the Association of Serbs in Austria. Inside, the walls were plastered with campaign posters, slogans, and portraits of Serbia’s long-serving president, Aleksandar Vučić, and his ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).
