title: Socialists push for EU law on deepfakes
content:
BRUSSELS — European legislators are calling for EU-wide regulations to ban noxious deepfakes and hold technology platforms responsible for preventing their spread.

A draft of the tech objectives of the center-left Socialists and Democrats group in the European Parliament, seen by POLITICO, calls for a ban on harmful, non-consensual or deceptive deepfakes — a move that would require platforms and AI providers to prevent their spread rather than wait for victims to complain.

The push comes amid a Europe-wide debate over who controls a person’s digital identity as AI increasingly allows for the easy production of everything from a politician’s fake endorsement to the clone of your neighbor’s voice to pull off a scam. Denmark this month introduced a plan to amend its copyright law to bar sharing digital replicas without consent. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni applied to trademark a recording of her voice to protect against unauthorized use.

Despite the increased public attention and legislative activity, competing laws across borders could allow deepfakes to proliferate and make enforcement difficult both for platforms and authorities.

title: Elderly women are often victims of gender-based violence. Why is it so hard for them to get help?
content:
In 1997, Ana Orantes appeared on an Andalusian television programme to recount a lifetime of abuse at the hands of her husband. Just a few days after her harrowing testimony, she was brutally murdered by her abuser. Her case prompted a widespread reckoning on gender-based violence in Spain, which led to significant legislative reforms.

Ana Orantes died at the age of 60 as an elderly woman who had suffered violence and abuse for 40 years. But today, despite the impact that her case had, older victims of gender-based violence remain marginalised, to the point of being practically invisible. They do not fit the social stereotype of a victim, which we tend to associate with a young woman, often with young children in her care.

But while gender-based violence affects all kinds of women, of all ages and from all walks of life, not all victims find themselves in the same circumstances. And for any intervention to work, it must take this complex reality into account.

Elder gender-based abuse often merges two realities: domestic violence stretching back years or decades, and abuse of older people associated with dependence and care, often in the form of neglect or psychological abuse.

title: Palestinian citizens face a painful choice in Israel’s election: To vote or not
content:
Elections are typically framed as a choice for voters. For Palestinian citizens of Israel, however, the country’s national ballots pose more of a dilemma.

Constituting about one-sixth of eligible voters in Israel, Palestinian citizens could hold the difference in a race expected to be close. But voting involves a trade-off: By casting a ballot for their best interests, many Palestinian citizens believe they also risk legitimizing a process that seeks to silence their voice and a system that treats their citizenship as conditional.

The coming Israeli election on Oct. 27, 2026, brings that tension to a new peak. Since the last general election in 2022, the destruction and mass killing in Gaza, restrictions on Palestinian citizens’ speech and protest and leading opposition parties’ rejection of having Arab political partners have sharpened the dilemma of seeking protection through institutions that reinforce their exclusion.

Having devoted most of my academic career to studying relations between Israel and its Palestinian citizens, I see the question facing Palestinian citizens of Israel as part of a much longer struggle over survival, citizenship and political belonging.

title: Become Part of the Legacy of Abolitionist and Educator, Myrtilla Miner
content:
Today’s post is from Lauren Algee, a Senior Digital Collections Specialist & By the People community manager at the Library of Congress. 

In 1851, more than a decade before the Emancipation Proclamation was issued, the School for Colored Girls opened in Washington, D.C. with the mission of training Black women educators. The institution was the first of its kind in the District and only the fourth in the nation. Today, the Library of Congress and the By the People volunteer transcription program invite you to celebrate the life and legacy of its courageous and barrier-breaking founder, Myrtilla Miner (1815-1864).

Miner spent her young adulthood teaching in New York, Rhode Island, and Mississippi. In the latter she was denied permission to conduct classes for enslaved children, after which she resolved to open her own school for “colored” women teachers. 

Frederick Douglass recalled that when she came to him asking for support for her endeavor, he “thought the proposition was reckless, almost to the point of madness” but “her resolution was taken, and was not to be shaken or changed.”

title: Nicaragua ja Ortega – toksinen ja päättymätön liittouma
content:
Nicaraguan demokratian ja ihmisoikeuksien tilanne on heikentynyt vuosi vuodelta samalla kun vanheneva presidentti Daniel Ortega rajoittaa kansalaisten vapauksia ja viitoittaa tietä luovuttaakseen vallan lopullisesti kanssahallitsija-vaimolleen Rosario Murillolle. Niskassa painavat Somozan diktatuurin muistot, sandinistisen vallankumouksen valuviat ja myrskyisät suhteet Yhdysvaltoihin. 

Artikkeliin on haastateltu kirjoittajan nicaragualaista ystävää, joka asuu maassa.

Nicaragualla on poikkeuksellisen väkivaltainen poliittinen historia ja pitkä kokemus sekä diktatuurista, vallankumouksesta että Yhdysvaltain vaikutuksesta. Itsenäistymisen jälkeen 1900-luvun alussa Nicaragua oli Yhdysvaltojen hallinnassa, ja miehitys päättyi Anastasio Somoza Garcian valtaannousuun. Somoza käynnisti 70 vuotta kestäneen sortavan diktatuurin, joka päättyi vuoden 1979 vallankumoukseen sandinistien johdolla.

title: Väitös: Taiteilijoiden kiinnittyminen monialaisiin työyhteisöihin vaatii toimintaprosessien selkiyttämistä
content:
Taiteilijoiden osaaminen kiinnostaa erityisesti sosiaali-, terveys- ja hoiva-alojen työyhteisöjä. Taiteilijoiden soveltavilla työskentelymenetelmillä voidaan vahvistaa organisaatioiden kulttuurihyvinvointiin liittyvää osaamista sekä uudistaa työarjen käytäntöjä sosiaalisesti kestävämpään suuntaan. TaM Niina Oinas on kehittänyt väitöstutkimuksessaan prosessimallin, jolla taiteilijoiden monialaista yhteistyötä voitaisiin vahvistaa.

Jo useamman vuosikymmenen ajan kansalliset ja kansainväliset tutkimukset ovat osoittaneet taiteilijoiden osaamisen vahvistavan useita eri toimialoja, erityisesti kohtaavassa työssä. Erilaiset hierarkioista vapaat, taideperustaiset toimintamallit ovat osoittautuneet tehokkaiksi uudistamisen työvälineiksi erityisesti sosiaali-, terveys- ja hoiva-aloilla. title: Do we really need all this cheese water?
content: A spoonful of whey in your morning cereal, a protein shake after an intense leg session. For many of us, focusing on protein in our diets has become a habit. Fewer of us know where the protein taking over our supermarkets actually comes from. Gym-goers' favourite product, whey powder, is a by-product of cheesemaking: it starts as the yellowish liquid left over after milk is thickened into curds and strained. That liquid is then dried into powder. Whey keeps most of milk’s lactose and water-soluble vitamins and about a fifth of its protein. For centuries, people drank it (for example the Scottish whey wine called “blaand“) or used it as a medicine for gut health. Today, up to 200 million tonnes of whey are produced as a by-product of industrial cheesemaking globally. The European Union alone makes more than a quarter of it. The hype around high-protein food has increased demand for whey, but production volumes have stayed the same, as they're linked to cheese production. As a result, the price of whey has skyrocketed in Europe in recent months. About a third of Europeans – and especially younger people – want to increase their protein intake, according to a recent survey by the EIT

title: NATO Must Prepare for Russian Missile Swarms
content:
Low-cost Russian cruise missiles are the latest evolution of the Russian airborne threat. They are substantially cheaper than the higher-end legacy cruise missiles and, at the same time, they are more powerful and lethal than the masses of long-range drones Russia has so far relied on for saturation strikes.

As a result, Russia has found a new cost-effective, mass-produced tool to overwhelm Ukraine’s air defenses and pummel its critical infrastructure. It would be wrong, however, to assume that these missiles challenge only Ukraine. In a direct confrontation with Russia, European NATO states would be equally ill-prepared.

Russia’s shift from long-range drones to low-cost cruise missiles began with Geran-3. The Geran-3 was functionally very similar to the Geran-2 long-range drone but replaced its piston engine with a JT80 turbojet produced by the Chinese manufacturer Telefly. This roughly doubled the system’s speed from 185 kph to 350 kph (115 mph to 214 mph) and raised its cruising altitude from 4,000 meters to 7,000 meters (13,000 ft. to 23,000 ft.), allowing it to escape existing Ukrainian long-range drone defenses.

title: Nobel Peace Laureate Navi Pillay on ICC, Gaza, Rape as War Crime, Her South African Roots & Mandela
content:
We speak with the acclaimed South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hours after Pillay was announced as winner of the Nobel Prize, the United States imposed sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court.

“It’s extremely shocking to me, totally unacceptable, that the United States administration can today impose sanctions against the International Criminal Court,” says Pillay, speaking to Democracy Now! from The Hague.

title: Third meeting: Information integrity in the age of AI, from manipulation to regulatory responses
content:
The Workstream on Safeguarding Access to Reliable Information in the Age of AI held its third meeting on 1 October 2026. Co-chaired by Luxembourg, Spain and Ukraine, the closed-door online session brought together representatives of signatory States of the Partnership for Information and Democracy, civil society and researchers. The discussion focused on information integrity and manipulation: the technical challenges identified, the open questions for research, regulatory gaps and the policy responses emerging across regions.

Key insights from researchers, government and regulatory authorities

How AI is changing manipulation

The first half of the meeting focused on the issues at stake, looking at how AI also affects and distorts the flow of information itself through algorithmic gatekeeping, influence operations, and manipulation. It is increasingly used to sow distrust, to emphasize some views for political gain, or, as some speakers emphasized for economic gain.

title: Guatemala: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer Fatally Shot
content:
(Washington, DC) – Guatemalan authorities should carry out a thorough, prompt, and credible investigation into the killing of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, a prominent anti-corruption lawyer, former prosecutor, and former head of Guatemala’s tax agency, Human Rights Watch said today.

On October 17, 2026, armed assailants shot and killed Solórzano Foppa at the Campo Marte sports complex in Guatemala City. Another man, identified by authorities as Gustavo Adolfo Aguilar Gamarro, was also killed in the attack. Guatemalan authorities arrested two men in connection with the crime, but prosecutors said there was no evidence linking them to the attack and a judge ordered their release. 

“The killing of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa is a shocking attack against a lawyer who played a prominent role in some of Guatemala’s most important anti-corruption efforts,” said Juanita Goebertus, Americas director at Human Rights Watch. “Guatemalan authorities should ensure a thorough, prompt, and credible investigation capable of identifying not only the gunmen, but also anyone who planned, ordered, or facilitated this crime.”

title: Decoding Pro-Israel Buzzwords in a Time of Genocide

By Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Nearly two years ago, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International released in-depth reports documenting that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Months later, Israeli human rights groups did likewise. Support for Israel has declined steeply among Americans, but its defenders continue to maintain a siege of buzzwords against Palestinian rights.

As historian Rashid Khalidi emphasized in his book Brokers of Deceit: How the U.S. Has Undermined Peace in the Middle East, “language matters.” Standard terms and tropes “are the essential building blocks of a lofty and solid edifice of denial of an entire narrative, of the existence of an entire people, which is basic to the affirmation of a formidable counterreality.”

Prominent groups, notably the Anti-Defamation League, the American Jewish Committee, AIPAC and Christians United for Israel – along with allies in Congress, the Executive Branch and the punditocracy – rely on the same buzzwords to defame critics of Israel and deny its systematic crimes against Palestinian people. title: Illustrated concert: Žižek Says!
content:
Concert: Žižek Says!

Thursday, 12 November 2026 at 8pm

An exceptional concert at Institut finlandais, illustrated by Ville Ranta, who has won awards for his bold comics, draws the concert for the audience, his illustrations based on expressive contemporary musical works. In a tumultuous duo, accordionist Niko Kumpuvaara and singer-saxophonist Joonatan Rautiola paint surrealist utopias by blending Finnish, French and Ukrainian music. 

The main work of the concert Žižek Says! is a musical theatre performance about power: the musicians try to bluff each other by playing inaccurately, the instruments are moved like puppets and in the end, the singing voice takes over the musician’s body as if in a Žižekian psychoanalysis. In this work played here for a world premiere at Institut finlandais, composer Miika Hyytiäinen combines humour with the savage possibilities of the human voice and experimental musical theatre.

title: Albanian PM Offers Dialogue Amid Crackdown on Violent Protests
content:
After months of public unrest and more than a week of escalating anti-government protests, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama has called demonstrators to the negotiating table, setting up chairs labeled "DIALOGUE" at the bottom of the stairs leading into the government building. 

"Now, whoever wants unconditional dialogue, wherever they want, whenever they want, even here if they want, I am available along with the Government," Rama said in a video posted to Facebook on Tuesday. "The only ones who are not welcome are those who commit violence and those who do not distance themselves from violence."

The overture comes as student-led demonstrations enter their eighth day, with crowds demanding Rama's resignation over allegations of widespread corruption. During a meeting with education officials, Rama characterized the recent unrest as a "hybrid war," claiming that foreign and political actors are exploiting genuine economic concerns to incite violence and attempt to overthrow the government.

Meanwhile, the streets of Tirana have seen severe clashes, with demonstrators throwing stones and firecrackers at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.

title: Hear How Clare Torry’s Vocals on Pink Floyd’s “The Great Gig in the Sky” Made the Song Go from Pretty Good to Downright Great
content:
Smack in the middle of Pink Floyd’s classic Dark Side of the Moon sits a song many listeners may hear as an extended bridge between the two true centerpieces, “Time” and “Money.” But I’ve always thought of “The Great Gig in the Sky” as the album’s true center, a swirling, swinging, soulful prog-rock masterpiece, carried to stratospheric heights by British singer Clare Torry. The song’s wordless gospel vocal makes it an ecstatic, even hopeful, tent pole supporting Dark Side’s brilliantly cynical songs about the banality and injustice of modern life.

“The Great Gig in the Sky,” that is to say, provides much-needed emotional release in an album that can sound, writes Alexis Petridis, “like one long sigh.” Yet if you know the story of Dark Side of the Moon and of Clare Torry’s defining contribution, you’ll know that her incredible soaring vocal was sheer happenstance, an improvisation by a young singer brought in at the last minute by producer Alan Parsons—and one who wasn’t a particular fan of the band. (“If it had been The Kinks,” she remembered, “I’d have been over the moon.”)

title: Hyljekarkottimet ehkäisivät kalastajien verkkovaurioita Naantalinaukolla
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tutkimuksessa akustisten hyljekarkotinten soveltuvuutta kokeiltiin ensimmäistä kertaa kokonaisen merenlahden mittakaavassa. Naantalinaukolla toteutetun tutkimuksen tulokset viittaavat siihen, että hylkeet vaurioittivat kaupallisten kalastajien verkkoja harvemmin karkotinten ollessa käytössä.

Luonnonvarakeskus (Luke) tutki vuosina 2018–2025 akustisten hyljekarkotinten käyttöä Naantalinaukolla. Noin 40 neliökilometrin laajuiselle lahtialueelle johtaviin kapeisiin salmiin sijoitettiin karkotinlaitteita, joiden avulla hylkeiden pääsyä alueelle pyrittiin estämään.

Naantalinaukolla toimii useita aktiivisia kaupallisia kalastajia. Alue on myös tärkeä virkistyskalastusalue ja kuhan lisääntymisalue. Keskeisin kalastettava laji on kuha, mutta alueella kalastetaan paljon myös ahventa, haukea ja siikaa. Hylkeet ovat haitanneet erityisesti Naantalinaukon verkkokalastusta.

Tutkimus oli ensimmäinen laatuaan näin laajassa mittakaavassa. Luke toteutti sen yhteistyössä Suomen Ammattikalastajaliiton ja paikallisten kalastajien kanssa.

title: Vihreät pitää paikkansa myönteisyysmittauksessa, kokoomus romahti imagovertailussa vihreiden taakse
content:
Vihreät on kolmen myönteisimmin arvioidun puolueen joukossa, kertoo Verianin tuore Puoluebarometri. SDP:hen suhtautuu myönteisesti 48 prosenttia suomalaisista ja keskustaan 43 prosenttia. Vihreät on kolmantena 41 prosentilla, ja sen perässä tulevat vasemmistoliitto, jonka arvioi positiivisimmaksi 38 prosenttia vastaajista, sekä Liike Nyt, 36 prosenttia.

Kokoomus ylsi vasta kuudennelle sijalle. Pääministeripuolueesta myönteisen käsityksen omaa 32 prosenttia, RKP:stä 29, perussuomalaisista 27 ja kristillisdemokraateista 24 prosenttia vastaajista.

Vihreiden myönteinen arvio on parantunut hieman kevään mittauksesta. Samaan suuntaan ovat kehittyneet myös SDP, perussuomalaiset, kristillisdemokraatit ja vasemmistoliitto. Suurin muutos on Liike Nytillä, jonka myönteisten arvioiden osuus kasvoi yhdeksän prosenttiyksikköä. Keskustaan ja kokoomukseen suhtaudutaan nyt hieman kielteisemmin kuin puoli vuotta sitten.

Kuvaa täydentää Verianin tekemä imagotutkimus, jonka muun muassa Yle ja Iltalehti ovat saaneet. Tutkimuksen tilaavat eduskuntapuolueet osana puoluebarometria, eikä sitä ole tarkoitettu julkisuuteen. Iltalehti uutisoi imagotuloksista ensimmäisenä.

title: Elected women never asked to be nudified, yet here we are
content: As a person of a marginalised gender, existing online means being constantly amazed by all the ways the internet can be used against you, no matter how powerful you are. One of the latest additions to that arsenal are “nudification” apps, AI-powered tools that can be prompted to create fake, sexually explicit pictures and videos of people, usually without their consent. All you need is a single photo of them. Two recent reports by Berlin thinktank Agora Digitale Transformation looked at how these tools are affecting politicians. The first one found 147 members of national European parliaments were either directly depicted in fake nudes or listed on sites that help people create them. Unsurprisingly, women were far more likely to be affected than men – 33 times more likely, in fact. Surprisingly, political affiliation hardly affected who was targeted, but seniority did. People in more prominent positions were more likely to be affected. title: ‘Reverse-Engineer Anything’ Is the New Wild West of AI
content:
Over the weekend, it became fashionable to use AI to replace the operating systems on smart TVs with vibe coded or AI reverse-engineered ones to make them less bloated. People have taken proprietary internet-of-things devices that were bricked and abandoned by their creators and used AI to hack them and install new software on them, giving functionality the original developers took away.  

In the last few days I have seen people hack smart picture frames to become AI-powered smart calendars, baby monitors to remove all ads, and bricked Lululemon mirrors to bring them back to life with new software. And dozens and dozens of TVs to install AI-written software that removes bloatware, ads, and simplifies the user interface.

title: Hunger Amid Plenty Is a Political Failure, UN Rights Chief Warns
content:
The world produces more than enough food, yet conflict, inequality, waste and the concentration of farmland leave billions without an adequate diet.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — The world’s farms produce more food than ever before. The average global supply now exceeds 3,000 calories per person a day. Yet more than a quarter of humanity cannot regularly obtain enough food—or food of sufficient quality—to live a healthy life.

For UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, this contradiction makes hunger more than a humanitarian emergency. It is evidence of economic and political systems that fail to distribute the world’s abundance fairly.

Addressing the UN-hosted Committee on World Food Security in Rome on 19 October, Türk described hunger as an avoidable tragedy. The international community, he argued, already possesses the food, knowledge and resources needed to prevent it.

What is missing is the political determination to make the right to food a reality.

The scale of global food production challenges the long-standing assumption that hunger is mainly caused by shortages.

The world produces more than enough food, yet conflict, inequality, waste and the concentration of farmland leave billions without an adequate diet.

title: South Pacific Ponzi Scam “King” Noah Musingku Dies
content:
A fugitive South Pacific Ponzi scammer—who later proclaimed himself “king” of a remote armed territory at the center of Papua New Guinea’s Bougainville island—has been given a royal burial following his death from an unspecified illness, according to local media and photographs of the funeral posted on social media.

Noah Musingku was accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from victims across the region in a 1990s pyramid scheme known as U-Vistract. Following the collapse of the scheme, Musingku fled in the early 2000s to his home island of Bougainville, a region then still recovering from a devastating decade-long civil war.

Styling himself as King David Peii II of the twin kingdoms of Papaala and Me’ekamui, Musingku set up a pseudo-state with its own armed militia, banking system, and local currency known as the Bougainville kina (BVK). The BVK was later declared illegal by Papua New Guinea’s government.

title: New long-clawed British dinosaur is the first of its kind in Europe
content:
The fossilised skull of a new species of mysterious meat-eating dinosaur from the Isle of Wight has been rediscovered in the collections of the Natural History Museum after over 100 years in storage.

Over its nearly 150-year history, this London museum has become home to over 30 million specimens, making it fairly easy to forget about the odd fossil or rock here and there. This is almost definitely what happened to the only known fossil of the UK’s newest dinosaur, a two-legged meat-eating theropod (the dinosaur family including birds) which we have named Invictibellatrix amberina in a new study.

title: Pelko koneiden ylivallasta syntyi jo 200 vuotta sitten – uutuuskirja paljastaa tekoälyn romanttiset juuret
content:
Tekoälyn historia alkaa kauan ennen tietokoneita. Uusi kulttuurihistoriallinen teos tutkii ajattelevien koneiden kulttuurihistoriaa 1600-luvulta 1840-luvulle. Erityisesti romantiikan ajan kirjallisuus ja filosofia auttavat ymmärtämään, mistä nykyiset koneälyyn liittyvät toiveet ja kauhukuvat ovat peräisin.

"Romantikot pelkäsivät koneiden ottavan vallan ihmisistä. Tunnetuin esimerkki tästä on Mary Shelleyn romaani Frankenstein, jossa tiedemiehen valmistama keinotekoinen olento karkaa laboratoriosta. Koneälyn uhka ja lupaus kasvoivat yhdessä", kulttuurihistorian dosentti Nivala sanoo Turun yliopiston tiedotteessa.

Ajattelevien koneiden historiaan kuuluu myös näyttäviä huijauksia. Romantiikan ajan yleisöjä hämmästytti Turkkilainen shakkikone, joka näytti pelaavan shakkia itsenäisesti. Todellisuudessa siirroista vastasi laitteen sisään piilotettu ihminen.

title: We brought back the lynx, but will we save the rest?
content: When Portuguese biologist Henrique Pereira was a kid in the 1980s, there were almost no vultures left in southern Europe. Now, “you cannot drive more than a few days in Portugal or Spain without seeing vultures flying over,” he told The European Correspondent. “There was a huge recovery.” The professor of biodiversity conservation at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg told The European Correspondent about the success stories of European wildlife recovery: bears, lynxes, and wolves, for example. Wildlife that was once close to extinction made a comeback. A new WWF report looks into global wildlife loss and paints a less pretty picture: the size of global vertebrate wildlife populations has shrunk by an average of 73% since 1970. Sabien Leemans, biodiversity manager at WWF EU, noted that “in Europe, industrial development started way before 1970. title: Scientists Discover A Strange Particle Explains the Origin of Reality
content:
Scientists have discovered that an exotic particle that existed at the birth of the universe might solve one of the biggest mysteries in cosmology and help explain reality as we know it, according to a new study in Physical Review Letters.

Our modern universe is dominated by matter, but it also contains fleeting amounts of antimatter, which is like a bizarro version of matter made of particles with the same mass, but opposite electrical charges. For instance, matter contains positively-charged protons and negatively-charged electrons, whereas antimatter is made up of the inverse: negatively-charged antiprotons and positively-charged positrons. 

As a result of these opposite features, matter and antimatter particles annihilate each other when they meet. This mutual destruction is the source of a major cosmic mystery, given that equal amounts of matter and antimatter are predicted to have formed in the split-seconds following the Big Bang. Yet somehow, matter emerged as the far more dominant substance in the cosmos, an asymmetry that has yet to be explained.

title: Germany’s Colonial Reckoning Returns to the Bundestag
content:
Debate over the genocide committed in Namibia has revived questions about recognition, reparations and whether Germany is willing to confront its colonial past as seriously as other chapters of its history.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Over a century after German colonial troops committed mass killings in what is now Namibia, the subject has resurfaced in the Bundestag with significant political momentum.

The whole thing was kicked off by an opposition motion calling for Germany to recognise the genocide against the Ovaherero and Nama unambiguously and to go beyond development aid to what the proponents would describe as restorative justice. DW reported on the ensuing parliamentary debate and the long-standing dispute over recognition and reparations.

title: I’m a CTO. AI still needs your human expertise | Madhu Shashanka
content:
AI is increasingly getting good at doing some tasks, but it can never replace human workers’ judgment

Autonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. While Waymos crash far less often than human drivers over tens of millions of miles, they’re still terrible at performing basic tasks – keeping out of disabled parking spots and tow-away zones, or steering clear of a church garage during Sunday service, according to the Wall Street Journal.

That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. And it has implications for what work will remain human and what will be automated by AI.

Madhu Shashanka is co-founder, chief scientist and chief technology officer at Concentric AI, a data security software company

content:
Karvin loppuvuoden 2026 julkistukset esittelevät ajankohtaista arviointitietoa eri koulutusasteilta. title: 'It Ain't Right:' Texas Said It Would Halt Data Center Permits. The State is Pushing Ahead Anyway
content:
A group of Texans believe they’ve discovered evidence that the state’s environmental regulatory agency has continued to issue permits to data centers despite Governor Greg Abbott’s call for it to stop. 

The nonprofits Public Citizen and FracTracker Alliance, working with local activists in Texas, looked through the public database of the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) and discovered that the organization has worked on multiple permits for data center projects since Abbott called for a pause in the process on September 21. Abbott’s office denied approving any new permits in a statement to 404 Media. 

According to Public Citizen and the FracTracker Alliance, which cite documents publicly available on the TCEQ’s website, the agency has reviewed documents and assigned engineers related to more than a dozen permits related to data center projects in the state. Public Citizen listed more than 15 and the Fractracker Alliance found 35. The same day the nonprofits announced their findings, The Texas Tribune published a report that Abbott had received $9 million in donations from developers and owners of data centers.

title: Russian Strikes Rise Across NATO’s Eastern Flank
content:
There have been at least 17 attacks on NATO’s frontline states and Moldova in the past month, either with proven or suspected Russian direction.

The alliance’s political leaders and military commanders now face a deteriorating picture, with some member states on the Black Sea making urgent appeals for military support, including combat aircraft and anti-drone systems.

Russia’s campaign still uses so-called sub-threshold attacks that are provocative and damaging, even lethal, while remaining just short of triggering NATO’s Article 5 common defense. But Russia’s behavior is becoming more reckless, as with the attempt to destroy aircraft at Leipzig airport in August and attacks on merchant shipping (detailed below). The pattern is also notable for attacks on Elon Musk’s Starlink system, seen as critical to the operations of the Ukrainian Armed Forces.

Here are some of the most recent incidents:

Poland. September 23: Starlink terminal outside Warsaw set on fire. Polish government says Russian involvement likely.

Moldova. October 3: Three Russian missiles and two drones entered Moldovan airspace. Debris found on Moldovan soil.
snippet: There have been at least 17 attacks on NATO’s frontline states and Moldova in the past month, either with proven or suspected Russian direction.

title: The future of early cancer detection with metamaterial technology and artificial intelligence
content:
Early detection and effective treatment of cancer are critical to improving patient survival outcomes. The rapid advancement of machine learning (ML), particularly deep learning, has led to significant improvements in the accuracy and efficiency of cancer screening, detection, and monitoring.

However, despite these advances, ML-based approaches face a significant limitation: the substantial computational resources required for the analysis and interpretation of medical images.

Detecting cancer at the earliest possible stage gives patients the best chance of successful treatment. Early diagnosis improves outcomes by enabling timely access to care and is therefore a critical public health strategy in all settings.

title: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer in Guatemala Assassinated
content:
The prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa was fatally shot along with another man on Saturday at a sports center in Guatemala City. For years, Solórzano Foppa had been outspoken against Guatemala’s most powerful politicians, business leaders and companies. He was known for his anti-corruption work as head of the Criminal Investigations Directorate within the Public Prosecutor’s Office and later as head of Guatemala’s tax authority, when he helped prosecute dozens of powerful Guatemalan business figures.

“In more recent years, he developed a social media presence, and he was forcefully denouncing corruption,” says Roman Gressier, a journalist based in Guatemala City. “We were thinking about [the killing of Solórzano Foppa] not only as an assassination, but also having a deep effect on freedom of expression.”

“Juan Francisco was a young lawyer coming from a background of pro-democracy and revolutionary activists,” says Silvia Solórzano Foppa, Juan Francisco’s mother. Her son was 43 years old when he was killed.

title: Require Police to Get a Warrant to Search ALPR Data
content:
This post was co-written by Andi Cao, an EFF legal intern.

Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are mass surveillance. They photograph every passing car and log where and when it was captured, building a searchable record of where nearly everyone drives. Cities should not buy them, and cities that already have them should shut them down.

Where these systems still operate, courts and state legislatures must reduce their harms by (among other things) requiring police to get a warrant before searching stored ALPR data. A warrant requirement would not make mass surveillance acceptable, but it would require police to justify a search to a judge before accessing records of people’s movements. Without this independent judicial check on police power, officers have been searching this data for improper reasons (many exposed by EFF) that violate our fundamental rights.

content: Komission ehdotuksella uudistetaan EU:n yleistä päästökauppajärjestelmää (EU ETS) vuoden 2030 jälkeiselle ajalle. Ehdotuksen tavoitteena on saattaa päästökauppa linjaan EU:n vuoden 2040 ilmastotavoitteen kanssa sekä samalla huomioida eurooppalaisen teollisuuden kilpailukyky ja hiilivuotoriskit. Ehdotus on laaja. Se sisältää muun muassa muutoksia päästöoikeuksien kokonaismäärään ja markkinavakausvarantoon, ilmaisjakoon, kansainvälisten ilmastoyksiköiden ja pysyvien hiilenpoistojen käyttöön sekä päästökauppatulojen käyttöön ja uusiin rahastoihin. Lisäksi päästökaupan soveltamisalaa laajennettaisiin meri- ja lentoliikenteessä sekä yhdyskuntajätteen polttoon. Tässä lausunnossa keskitytään päästöoikeuksien kokonaismäärään, teollisuuden ilmaisjakoon sekä innovaatiotukeen ja teollisuuden vähähiilistämispankkiin.

title: Enkät: Sverigefinsk litteratur – de viktigaste verken för dig?
content:
Vilka är de viktigaste verken inom den sverigefinska litteraturen? Finlandsinstitutets bibliotek har lanserat en enkät riktad till sverigefinnar för att identifiera verk som är viktiga för minoriteten. De böcker som föreslås ska vara skrivna av författare med finsk bakgrund bosatta i Sverige. Utifrån enkäten kommer en litteraturlista att tas fram som stöd för bibliotekens beståndsarbete.

Vilka sverigefinska böcker har varit betydelsefulla för dig? Vilka verk av sverigefinska författare skildrar bäst minoritetens språk, kultur, identitet och erfarenheter i Sverige?

Finlandsinstitutets bibliotek vill ha hjälp av sverigefinnar att identifiera centrala verk inom den sverigefinska litteraturen. Vi välkomnar tips på böcker som belyser minoritetens erfarenheter och historia. Du kan föreslå till exempel romaner, noveller, dikter och facklitteratur.

Målet är att sammanställa en litteraturlista med centrala verk inom den sverigefinska litteraturen för bland annat bibliotekens användning. De förslag som samlas in genom enkäten kommer att ligga till grund för ett expertmöte där listan kompletteras med forskningsbaserad kunskap.

title: Saudi Arabia: Man Executed for Childhood Offenses
content:
(Beirut) – Saudi authorities announced on October 17, 2026, that they had executed Hassan Zaki al-Faraj, who was convicted of crimes allegedly committed when he was a 14-year-old boy, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Supreme Court has also apparently upheld the death sentence of another man, Yousef al-Manasif, who was convicted of crimes allegedly committed when he was 15 and 16, putting him at risk of imminent execution. At least three other men convicted of alleged crimes committed as children are on death row, despite allegations of torture, forced confessions, and prolonged solitary confinement.

“The execution of Hassan al-Faraj is unconscionable compounded by alleged torture-tainted evidence and a well-documented record of unfair trials,” said Joey Shea, senior Saudi Arabia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “With the Supreme Court’s recent decision, Yousef al-Manasif is also at serious risk of execution.”

title: Decline of European Culture: Decadence, Hatred, and Incitement
content:
A commentary by Wolfgang Bittner*

GÖTTINGEN, Germany | 19 October 2026 (IDN) — Russia is to be defeated—at any cost. The Berlin government intends to continue supporting Ukraine in its war with weapons and funds at the expense of its own population, “for as long as necessary.” [1]

It is questionable how much longer this can go on. But in this situation, there is an opportunity to break free from vassalage and the US’s military and cultural stranglehold and rediscover one’s own cultural roots. The primary objective should be to establish Germany’s sovereignty and neutrality, which would allow many current problems to be resolved. This requires a fundamental policy shift.

With respect to the war in Ukraine, it is becoming increasingly clear that this is not merely a conflict between the Collective West and the Global South, including Russia, but, in the broadest sense, a clash between two cultural spheres: the decadent US-dominated Western culture and a historically grown conservative European culture.

title: Kolumnipajassa opit väistelemään tylsää kirjoittamista
content:
Miten syntyy kolumni, joka ei tyydy kädenlämpöiseen pyörittelyyn tai pelkkään kärjistettyyn mielipiteeseen?

Jokesin kaksipäiväisessä Kolumnipajassa kokeneet journalistit jakavat osaamistaan kolumnin ideoinnista, perusteluista, tekstin sävystä ja huumorista.  Kolumnipajan kouluttajina ovat mm. Reetta Räty, Anu Silfverberg, Adile Sevimli, Pekka Juntti ja Kuukausiliitteen Kuukautinen eli Teppo Sillantaus. 

”Kolumnin idea ei ole vain se, että kerrotaan jokin räväkkä mielipide”, sanoo Jokesinkaksipäiväisen pajan vetäjä Reetta Räty. ”Kolumni voi olla hyvinkin syvällinen tulkinta ajankohtaisista asioista, tai sitten hauska pläjäys, joka osuu ajanhermoon. Kolumni on uusi näkökulma, perusteltu mielipide. Se voi analysoida, luoda kontekstia, kuvata ajan henkeä, tapaa, menoa. Parhaimmillaan se saa ajattelemaan jotain uutta tai tuo päivänvaloon asian, joka on jäänyt varjoon. Ai noinkin voi olla! Tuollainen ajatus!”

Tammikuussa Helsingissä järjestettävään Kolumnipajaa valitaan 12 journalistia. Haku on parhaillaan käynnissä. 

Miksi toimittajan kannattaisi hakea Kolumnipajaan?

title: AI-kahvit: Tekoäly seniorien arjessa
content:
Tämä Teams-tallenne on osa AI-kahvit-sarjaa, jonka on tuottanut Yleisten kirjastojen tekoälyosaamisen kehittämishanke. AI-kahveilla pohditaan tällä kertaa, miten tekoäly näkyy ikääntyneiden arjessa, millaisia mahdollisuuksia, kysymyksiä ja huolia tekoälyn käyttöön liittyy seniorien näkökulmasta ja miten kirjasto voi tukea ikääntyneitä asiakkaita tekoälyn käytössä ja vahvistaa heidän tekoälylukutaitoaan.

Aiheesta puhuu SeniorSurf-toiminnan asiantuntija Eero Tuomenoksa. Hän kertoo, miten tekoäly on seniorien arjessa usein huomaamatta, esimerkiksi hakukoneiden tekoälyvastauksina ja puhelinten automaattivastaajina, ja millaisia kysymyksiä ja huolia ikääntyneillä on. Suurimmaksi huolenaiheeksi nousevat huijaukset. Tuomenoksa kannustaa rohkaisemaan seniorit kokeilemaan tekoälyä turvallisin periaattein: tekoäly toimii todennäköisyyslaskennan varassa, tärkeät asiat kannattaa tarkistaa, eikä henkilötietoja pidä syöttää. title: Naispuoliset moottoripyörätaksikuskit ovat Keniassa harvinaisia, mutta lasikaton murtajia löytyy – Loice Ambani ajoi synnyttämäänkin moottoripyörällä
content:
Länsi‑Kenian Kisumussa hiekka pöllyää ja torvet soivat. Paikallisbussien henkilökunta huutelee ohikulkijoita asiakkaikseen. Pian Quinter Jodo kaartaa paikalle tottunein ottein. Olemus on varma ja rauhallinen. Hän nostaa ajolasit pipon peittämälle otsalleen ja avaa toppatakkiaan. Vasta kun katse viipyy kuljettajassa pidempään, paljastuu seikka, joka saa osan asiakkaista epäröimään. Hän on nainen, ja se on harvinaista.

Jodo ajaa moottoripyörätaksia Länsi-Kenian Kisumussa. Victorianjärven rannalla sijaitseva Kenian kolmanneksi suurin kaupunki on vesi- ja rautatieyhteyksiensä ansiosta merkittävä solmukohta. Se tietää asiakasvirtoja myös boda­boda-­moottoripyörätaksikuskeille. Bodaboda-sana tulee enlanninkielisestä border to border -ilmaisusta, sillä mopotakseilla kuskattiin aikoinaan asiakkaita ja salakuljetettiin tavaroita Kenian ja Ugandan rajojen yli.

Kisumussa arvioidaan olevan jopa 130 000 moottoripyörätaksikuskia. Valtaosa kuljettajista on miehiä. Jodo ei tunne henkilökohtaisesti toisia naiskuljettajia, mutta on kuullut, että heitä on kaupungissa muuallakin.

title: Kaksi miljardia eläkkeistä? | Eläkeiän nosto | Eläkemaksuissa alennusvaraa
content:
Valtiovarainministeriön virkamiehet ehdottavat eläkeiän noston kiihdyttämistä. Kokoomus haluaa, että noin neljäsosa menosäästöistä, kaksi miljardia euroa, haetaan eläkkeistä. title: Kazakh President’s Grandnephew Donates Sport University to State Following Investigative Report
content:
Just one day after an investigation by Radio Azattyq and OCCRP, the grandnephew of Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced on Saturday that he is donating the Kazakh National University of Sports (KNUS) to the state.

Framing the handover as a patriotic gesture, Nurassyl Medeu stated the move was not a sale, a transfer into trust management, or a forced step, “but a gratuitous gift to my native country so that it prospers, reaches unprecedented heights, and achieves recognition at the global level.”

“Everything we created must serve our youth, our people, and our country,” he said, adding that it was a great honor to make the contribution. “If you compare KNUS to a ship, I built it to be powerful, reliable, and unbreakable.”

The unexpected announcement of Medeu followed a Friday investigation revealing Medeu to be the grandson of President Tokayev’s sister, Karlyga Izbastina, and detailing how two major educational ventures he founded received substantial state support.

title: The Dark Story Behind Edgar Allan Poe’s Most Famous Photograph, Taken Four Days After a Laudanum Overdose
content: In the Halloween season, one American writer comes to mind more often than any other: Edgar Allan Poe. That owes in large part to his famously macabre tales like “The Tell-Tale Heart,” “The Cask of Amontillado,” and “The Masque of the Red Death,” written though they may have been with barely concealed contempt for their sensation-seeking magazine readership. But it also has to do with the image of the man himself. Or rather, it has to do with one image in particular: a daguerreotype photograph taken on November 9, 1848, at a Providence studio that has inspired practically every representation of Poe in popular culture since.

title: For something to be feasible, it must be measurable! The ZenDiS Sovereignty Check
content:
German and European policymakers want us to achieve digital sovereignty. But what does that actually mean? When are we digitally sovereign, and what conditions must be met for that to happen?

The question, then, is: How do you actually measure digital sovereignty?

The Center for Digital Sovereignty in Public Administration (ZenDiS) addressed this question in the spring of 2026. To this end, ZenDiS developed a so-called “Sovereignty Check” for public administration. This check is based on clearly defined criteria across four categories, designed to make digital sovereignty measurable: –

  • Organization and Capabilities – An organization’s management and governance capabilities
  • Digital Applications and Services – the design and interchangeability of the applications used, as well as control over these applications
  • Information and Data – data ownership and data sovereignty
  • Operations and Infrastructure – technical and organizational operational sovereignty

title: The OTR Symposium 2026: Shaping the Open Transition takes place in one week!
content:
The first Open Technology Research (OTR) Symposium – the OTR Symposium 2026: Shaping the Transition – kicks off in one week, on 26 and 27 October 2026 at the University of Barcelona. The final agenda is now confirmed: three headline sessions, 18 research presentations across five thematic tracks and an open source hardware block, a panel on Barcelona’s own open transition, and the presentation of the Basil Cousins Award.

The OTR Symposium 2026 is convened by the founding members of Open Technology Research: OpenForum Europe, the Open Source Initiative, the Open Knowledge Foundation, and the Digital Infrastructure Insights Fund. It builds on OFE’s OpenForum Academy Symposium, which ran from 2021 to 2025, and takes place as part of Barcelona Open Tech Week. The Symposium is one of several events in Barcelona Open Tech Week, alongside Mozilla Festival, Decidim Fest, the 4D Conference, the Open Source Policy Summit and the Global Assembly for Open Source.

title: Citing ProPublica, Lawmakers Introduce Bill to Help U.S. Citizens Sue ICE for Wrongful Detentions
content:
What Happened: A New Mexico Democrat in the House introduced a bill last week that would make it easier for U.S. citizens to sue immigration agents and the federal government over wrongful detentions and arrests.

Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández credited ProPublica’s reporting as the catalyst for the bill, the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act. Earlier this month, we revealed that more than 500 U.S. citizens have been detained in warrantless arrests during the second Trump administration.

Leger Fernández said the legislation would roll back the protections from lawsuits that agents and the federal government currently have. It would also establish a minimum level of compensation for people who win their suits, and extend the statute of limitations for such cases.

The legislation would also take back any unspent Immigration and Customs Enforcement funding from President Donald Trump’s so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Leger Fernández’s bill was introduced with co-sponsor Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, a New Jersey Democrat.

    Sitran ja EVAn kyselytutkimus osoittaa, että suomalaiset suhtautuvat vihreään siirtymään kaksijakoisesti. Yhtäältä vastaajat pitävät ilmastonmuutoksen torjuntaa eurooppalaisena yhteishankkeena ja näkevät vihreässä siirtymässä myös taloudellisia mahdollisuuksia Suomelle. Toisaalta he kokevat, ettei EU:n energia- ja ilmastopolitiikka tunnista riittävästi Suomen erityisolosuhteita, ja pelkäävät tiukkojen ympäristötavoitteiden vaikutuksia eurooppalaisen teollisuuden kilpailukykyyn.

EU-tason ilmastopolitiikalle on vahva tuki, mutta kun siirrytään ilmastotavoitteista luonnonvaroihin, metsiin ja käytännön toimenpiteisiin, kansallisen liikkumatilan tarve kasvaa. Vihreä siirtymä hyväksytään, jos se näyttäytyy ilmastopoliittisesti välttämättömänä, taloudellisesti mahdollisena ja Suomen olosuhteet huomioivana.

title: Svensk innovation möter internationella affärsmöjligheter
content:
Vid mötet den 16 oktober deltog representanter för svenska storföretag och organisationer som arbetar med att främja svensk export, investeringar och innovation. Tillsammans med internationella företagsledare diskuterade de möjligheter och utmaningar inom den gröna omställningen.

Budskapet från svensk sida var tydligt: Sverige är öppet för samarbeten, investeringar och ökad handel.

Madeleine Sjöstedt, generaldirektör för Svenska institutet, betonade i sitt öppningsanförande att den gröna omställningen, hållbar tillväxt och tillgång till ny teknik kräver internationellt samarbete. Utmaningarna kan inte lösas av enskilda länder, företag eller organisationer, men de skapar samtidigt möjligheter till innovation, investeringar och nya affärer.

Genom att sammanföra beslutsfattare från olika länder med svenska företag och organisationer vill SI därför skapa kontakter som kan utvecklas till konkreta affärsmöjligheter.

title: After looting spree, France tells online resellers to crack down on traffic of stolen goods
content:
PARIS — The French government has called on leading online marketplaces such as Vinted and eBay to bar listings that include goods stolen during this weekend’s looting spree across France. 

“We expect these platforms to remove the listings in question without delay,” France’s Digital Affairs Minister Anne Le Hénanff wrote Monday in a post on X. “They will also be required to work closely with public authorities so that those reselling potentially stolen goods can be identified and prosecuted.”  

Le Hénanff and fellow cabinet members called a 7 p.m. meeting with representatives of Vinted, Amazon, eBay, Meta, and TikTok, as well as France’s leading independent reselling platform Leboncoin. 

During a government press conference earlier in the day, Minister for Small Businesses Serge Papin said officials were working on “coordination between investigators and online platforms” to identify the individuals behind suspicious listings. A specific protocol is expected to be put in place, according to a government source speaking to POLITICO.

title: Oral History and Heritage workshop in Monterrey
content:
On October 8 and 9, HERITΛGE held the in-person Oral History and Heritage workshop at the Museo Estatal de Culturas Populares de Nuevo León. The workshop – part of our HerMaP Mexico initiative – provided a space for learning and exchange focused on the use of oral history to document, preserve, and transmit cultural heritage and community memory. The program combined methodological tools, ethical considerations, and practical exercises applied to heritage projects.

The workshop brought together a group of eight participants working with Indigenous communities and cultural heritage projects, bringing diverse experiences and perspectives and representing at least five Indigenous peoples residing in Nuevo León. This exchange provided an opportunity to reflect on oral history not only as a documentation methodology, but also as a tool for strengthening the transmission of memories, knowledge, and living cultural practices.

title: Nuorten siirtymät työhön vaativat tukea, joka tunnistaa erilaiset tilanteet
content:
Nuorisotyöttömyys on pitkään ollut kasvussa. Heikko taloustilanne vaikeuttaa erityisesti nuorten siirtymää koulutuksesta työelämään, samalla kun työelämän kasvavat osaamisvaatimukset ja monimutkainen etuusjärjestelmä voivat tehdä siirtymästä entistä haastavamman. Työllistymistä tukevissa toimissa on tärkeää vahvistaa nuorten kouluttautumista, työ- ja toimintakykyä sekä luottamusta tulevaisuuteen. Työttömyysturvan tiukat ehdot ja sanktiot saattavat pahimmillaan ohjata nuoria tekemään järjestelmän ehtojen mukaisia valintoja, jotka heikentävät pidemmän aikavälin työmarkkina-asemaa.

Nuorten työllistymistä ja työelämään siirtymistä käsittelevässä Nuorisotutkimusseuran politiikkasuosituksessa korostetaan, että nuorten tilanteet ja tuen tarpeet vaihtelevat merkittävästi. Kasvavat osaamisvaatimukset vaikeuttavat erityisesti niiden nuorten työllistymistä, joilta puuttuu tutkinto, työkokemus tai riittävä työ- ja toimintakyvyn tuki. On tärkeää huomata, etteivät nuoret muodosta työmarkkinoilla yhtä ryhmää.

title: John J. Audubon’s Breathtaking Book of Birds
content:
—This is a guest post by Ashley Rose Young, a curator in the Rare Book and Special Collections Division. It also appears in the September/October issues of the Library of Congress Magazine.

In the early 19th century, John James Audubon set out to do something no natural history illustrator had attempted at such scale: depict North American birds at life size, in vivid, animated poses. The result was “The Birds of America,” one of the most ambitious — and physically imposing — sets of books ever produced.

Published between 1827 and 1838, the work was issued as a series of hand-colored engravings, printed on enormous “double elephant” sheets measuring roughly 38 by 26 inches. Audubon partnered with the London engraver Robert Havell Jr. to translate his paintings into prints of remarkable precision and color.

Subscribers received the plates in installments, eventually assembling a collection that included 435 illustrations depicting 489 species of birds. All that paper adds up: Typically bound in four volumes, “The Birds of America” can be astonishingly heavy. The Library’s set totals 196 pounds, with the largest volume weighing a whopping 55 pounds.

content:

title: Muinais-DNA paljastaa keskiaikaisen muuttoliikkeen Ruotsista Suomeen
content:
Uusi tutkimus Suomen väestöhistoriasta rautakauden lopulla ja keskiajalla paljastaa vilkkaat vuorovaikutusverkostot yli Itämeren. Turun yliopiston tutkimus analysoi Lounais-Suomessa ja Hämeessä 1000–1200-luvuilla eläneiden ihmisten perimää ja selvitti, miten alueen väestö muuttui keskiajan kuluessa ja millaisia yhteyksiä ihmisillä oli Itämeren muihin alueisiin.

Tulokset paljastavat merkittävän eron rannikon ja sisämaan väestöhistoriassa. Varhaiskeskiajalla (n. 1050–1250 jaa.) Lounais-Suomen rannikon ja sisämaan asukkaat olivat geneettisesti hyvin samanlaisia, vaikka alueilla oli kulttuurisia ja taloudellisia eroja. Tämän jälkeen kehitys kulki eri suuntiin: sisämaassa säilyi geneettinen jatkuvuus nykyaikaan saakka, kun taas rannikolla väestön geneettinen koostumus muuttui keskiajan jälkeen. Ruotsista saapuneen keskiaikaisen muuttoliikkeen vuoksi länsirannikon nykyisillä suomalaisilla on enemmän skandinaavista perimää kuin samalla alueella varhaiskeskiajalla eläneillä ihmisillä.

title: Tästä on kyse Eettisen kehityssanaston oppaassa
content:
Eettisen kehityssanaston oppaan perimmäisenä tarkoituksena on herättää ajatuksia kieleen linkittyvästä eriarvoisuudesta.

Jaa

Fingon julkaisema Eettisen kehityssanaston opas on herättänyt keskustelua. Kerromme tässä blogissa tarkemmin, mistä oppaassa on kyse ja oikaisemme väärinkäsityksiä.

Eettisen kehityssanaston opas ei kiellä tai pyri kieltämään minkään termin käyttöä – mutta se sisältää suosituksia perustelujen kera.

Kyseessä on nimenomaan opas, eikä kielenkäyttöä koskeva ohje. Oppaassa todetaan: ”Tärkeintä ei ole virheetön kielenkäyttö, vaan aito pyrkimys oppia ja ymmärtää kielessä ja sen rakenteissa piileviä ongelmia.”

Oppaassa on luokiteltu termejä kolmeen kategoriaan:

  • Yhdeksän käsitettä on luokiteltu kategoriaan Lakkaamme käyttämästä, joka määritellään seuraavasti: Nämä ovat termejä, joiden käyttämistä vältämme.
  • Kymmenen termiä on luokiteltu kategoriaan Herättää kysymyksiä. Se määritellään näin: Nämä ovat termejä, jotka herättävät kriittisiä kysymyksiä, mutta joiden käyttäminen voi silti olla tarkoituksenmukaista.

title: Police Say Scammers Used AI to Clone a Sheriff’s Voice
content:
A Florida police department claims that scammers used AI to clone a sheriff’s voice, with scammers increasingly using voice clones that trick people into thinking they’ve missed jury duty or have a warrant out for their arrest are increasing.

According to Florida news outlet News6, scammers cloned Osceola County Sheriff Steve Moser’s voice and left a voicemail with a resident.    

“They cloned his voice and was using Steve’s picture as well to say it was him making the phone call, and it was not,” Sheriff Chris Blackmon told News6.

Impersonating a police officer is a third-degree felony in Florida. The Osceola County sheriff’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

This particular scam cloning cops is spreading across several states, with reports of jury duty and arrest warrant scams targeting people in Georgia and Pennsylvania in the last week. These other reports don’t mention AI voice cloning explicitly, but note that the scammers sometimes have similar voices and tones as local police officers.

title: Human Rights Education Resources for Write for Rights 2026

Every year around 10 December – Human Rights Day – Amnesty International’s Write for Rights campaign brings millions of people together to stand in solidarity with individuals and communities facing human rights violations.

Around the world, people write letters, sign petitions, create artwork, learn together, and take action to demand justice. Year after year, these collective actions have helped change lives, showing that borders are no barrier to solidarity and that words have the power to inspire hope and drive change.

Human rights education is a central part of that movement. Alongside taking action, people come together to understand the issues behind each Individual at Risk case, reflect on why human rights matter and explore how solidarity can help protect them.

The Write for Rights 2026 Human Rights Education resources help teachers, educators and facilitators engage learners in meaningful learning about human rights and support them to take informed action.

title: It’s the Networks, Stupid
content:
It took Reform leader Nigel Farage less than 12 hours following Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s maiden speech at September’s UN General Assembly to falsely claim the UK’s new National Centre for Information Defence (NCID) would be a “Ministry of Truth to clamp down on free speech.”

Given that the scope and powers of NCID have yet to be determined, Farage’s comments had no evidential basis.

Burnham spoke of a center that would “detect, attribute and disrupt” hostile state attacks and an organization that would “support and defend our democracy.” The prime minister and officials who have worked on this announcement and will shape the eventual center should be congratulated on this move and supported in their efforts.

The “chiefs” tasked with shaping the center now have decisions to make in terms of the scope, scale, and priorities of NCID.

What are the key considerations?

Firstly, NCID will not decide what Britons are allowed to say. Genuine speech of any kind, along with domestic information manipulation activity (DIM), should not be within its scope.

title: Masked Israeli Settlers Nearly Kill Washington Post Journalist as Attacks on Palestinians Escalate
content: Israeli settlers backed by IDF soldiers brutally assaulted Palestinian olive farmers in the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, on Friday. Witnesses say dozens of masked Israeli settlers armed with clubs, sticks, slingshots and guns hurled rocks at Palestinian farmers, set olive trees ablaze and drove people from their fields. Veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a 64-year-old American, was documenting the attack when settlers began beating her. She suffered stab wounds, a broken rib, four broken vertebrae and a severe hand injury. Levine was wearing a clearly marked press vest and a helmet at the time of the attack. According to the Israeli human rights group Yesh Din, Israeli settlers have carried out at least 170 attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since September 27, which marked the start of this year’s olive harvest.

title: Lebanon: Amend Media Law to Protect Free Expression
content:
(Beirut) – Lebanon’s parliament should amend the recently-adopted media law to fully remove all provisions in Lebanese law that restrict the right to free expression, Human Rights Watch said today. Parliament passed the law on August 11, 2026, but a new draft law introduced by 10 members of parliament on October 5 offers amendments to the law that would resolve its key problematic provisions.

“Given the history of public officials and powerful individuals abusing Lebanon’s laws to clamp down on journalists, activists, and artists, parliament should act to prevent further abuse,” said Ramzi Kaiss, Lebanon researcher at Human Rights Watch. “No one should face abusive retaliation for peacefully expressing their views, and parliament has a chance to end these abuses right here and now.”

title: Five Questions About What’s Behind Nigeria’s Romance Scam Industry
content:
In February, OCCRP tracked down a 31-year-old man to his mansion in Nigeria’s capital Abuja. He had allegedly posed as the Crown Prince of Dubai to con a Romanian businesswoman out of more than $2.5 million in a romance scam, according to his victim and two accomplices. 

This is a well-trodden profession in Nigeria, where large numbers of young men, often facing extreme poverty, have taken to swindling lonely victims in wealthier countries to fill their pockets.  

Yet most of the romance scams originating in Nigeria are not particularly complex or lucrative, says journalist Carlos Barragán.

His recently published book, “The Yahoo Boys,” explores what drives the country's teenage fraudsters — whose nickname comes from the Yahoo email addresses used for “Nigerian prince” scams in the early days of the internet — and the repercussions of their scams in Nigeria and abroad.

title: When a Cat Co-Authored a Paper in a Leading Physics Journal (1975)
content:
Back in 1975, Jack H. Hetherington, a physics professor at Michigan State University, wrote a research paper on low–temperature physics for the respected scientific journal Physical Review Letters. Before sending it off, Hetherington asked a colleague to review the paper, just to make sure it covered the right bases. What happened next Hetherington explained in the 1982 book, More Random Walks in Science:

Before I submitted [the article], I asked a colleague to read it over and he said, ‘It’s a fine paper, but they’ll send it right back.’ He explained that that is because of the Editor’s rule that the word “we” should not be used in a paper with only a single author. Changing the paper to the impersonal seemed too difficult now, and it was all written and typed; therefore, after an evening’s thought, I simply asked the secretary to change the title page to include the name of the family cat, a Siamese called Chester, sired one summer by Willard (one of the few unfixed male Siamese cats in Aspen, Colorado). I added the initials F D in front of the name to stand for Felix Domesticus and thus created F D C Willard.

title: He Tried to Set Limits on His State’s School Vouchers. Billionaires Helped Bankroll a Campaign to Unseat Him.
content:
On a cold February morning at West Virginia’s Capitol, children in winter jackets, holding signs and their homework, clogged the hallways outside the House Finance Committee room. Delegate Vernon Criss, the committee’s chairperson, popped outside his office, then promptly walked back in. 

Five days earlier, the Republican lawmaker had proposed to limit payouts from a voucher program that diverts public tax dollars to private education. Since then, families had shown up each morning, and with them lobbyists and organizers posting inflammatory assertions that the proposal would kill the program.

Criss didn’t want that. Five years earlier, he voted to create the Hope Scholarship program, the nation’s first educational savings account program to have no income requirements. Since then, 11 other states have passed similar legislation.

title: France riots: Presidential hopeful Attal pitches social media blackout
content:
French presidential candidate Gabriel Attal reiterated his call to grant the government power to selectively block access to social media platforms to quell riots in the aftermath of widespread unrest across France over the weekend.

“You have young people at home who see their friends going out to loot, which gives the impression that they’re getting away with it; they see them on social media, and then they go out too,” Attal said in an interview with French radio station RTL.

Attal, a former prime minister who now leads French President Emmanuel Macron’s political party, said the measures must be “temporary” and “limited to the area where the riots are taking place.”

Saturday saw hundreds of thousands of protesters take to the streets nationwide across France, with students — who have been blockading schools in recent weeks to call for better study conditions, more teachers and more funding — joining trade unions and members of the public to protest the cost of living. While many protested peacefully, scenes of extreme violence also played out across the country. According to the latest figures from the interior ministry, some 2,000 people were arrested during the turmoil.

title: As French protests escalate into riots, they may prove a gift for Marine Le Pen’s right-wing party
content:
Mass protests in France have spiralled into riots, with between 500,000 and 800,000 demonstrators in cities and towns across the country, most of them students. More than 100 police and many more protesters have been injured and up to 2,000 people have so far been arrested.

Major public buildings – such as the town hall in Limoges and the historic tourist office in Lyon – were destroyed, while other public buildings were damaged and hundreds of shops were looted by small groups of mainly young men.

The protests began in the working-class suburb of Créteil in southeastern Paris on September 21 when high school students demonstrated against poor conditions: dilapidated facilities, a shortage of teachers and inconvenient timetabling (schools in France often spread classes between 8am and 6pm, including Saturday mornings, leaving one clear afternoon).

This summer’s heatwaves were still being felt in September in classrooms with no cooling systems. Senior school students have been further frustrated by the inefficiencies and inequities of the Parcoursup university application online portal.

title: Mitä valintoja tutkija tekee? – Jaana Vuoren uusi tiedeteos avaa empiiristä tutkimusta ihmistieteissä
content:
Sukupuolentutkimuksen professori emerita Jaana Vuoren uusi teos Johdatus empiiriseen tutkimukseen ihmistieteissä on kirjoitettu ensimmäiseksi korkeakoulutasoiseksi tutkimusmenetelmiä käsitteleväksi oppikirjaksi ihmistieteissä. Niitä ovat humanistiset ja yhteiskuntatieteet sekä monet tieteidenväliset alat.

Teos toimii myös käsikirjana pitemmälle ehtineille opiskelijoille ja tutkijoille sekä antaa virikkeitä menetelmien opettajille.

”Kirja on rakennettu tutkimusasetelman käsitteen varaan, sillä jokainen tutkimuksen tekijä ratkaisee siihen liittyviä kysymyksiä”, Jaana Vuori sanoo.

Mitä kaikkea voi käyttää aineistona? Millaista toimintaa on analysoiminen? Miksi tutkimuksen ytimessä on tutkimusongelma ja miten sellaisen voi keksiä? Miten ymmärtää teorian rooli analyysin ohjaajana? Miten päästä analyysin kautta tuloksiin ja tulkintoihin?

”Kirja tarjoaa näkökulmia ennen muuta siihen, millaisia valintoja tutkijat tekevät, jotta tutkimuksesta tulisi tuloksia ja tulosten pohjalta voitaisiin lisätä tietoa ympäröivästä maailmasta, ihmisten toiminnasta, yhteiskunnasta ja kulttuurista”, Jaana Vuori lisää.

Avainlippu on merkki suomalaisesta työstä. Merkin myöntämisen ensisijaisena kriteerinä on aina se, että tuote on valmistettu tai palvelu on tuotettu Suomessa. title: Virta: Hallitus murentaa oikeusvaltiota – syyttäjälaitoksen leikkaukset pysäytettävä
content:
Vihreiden puheenjohtaja Sofia Virta vaatii hallitusta perumaan oikeudenhoidon leikkaukset ja turvaamaan syyttäjälaitoksen resurssit. Hallituksen esitys pidentäisi syyteharkinta-aikaa ja kasvattaisi avoimien asioiden määrää.

Virran mukaan oikeus ei saa jäädä toteutumatta ruuhkien takia.

”Oikeusvaltio ei ole vain sitä, että meillä on riippumattomat tuomioistuimet ja laissa turvatut oikeudet. Oikeusvaltio tarkoittaa myös sitä, että rikokset tutkitaan, syytteet käsitellään ja ihmiset saavat asiansa ratkaistuksi kohtuullisessa ajassa. Jos rikoksen uhri tai rikoksesta epäilty joutuu odottamaan oikeutta vuosikausia, oikeusturva ei toteudu niin kuin sen pitäisi”, Virta sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Syyttäjälaitoksen tilanne on jo nyt vakava. Hallituksen omassa vuoden 2027 talousarvioesityksessä keskimääräiseksi syyteharkinta-ajaksi on kirjattu 5,6 kuukautta, kun vuonna 2025 se oli 2,7 kuukautta. Samalla avoimien asioiden määrän arvioidaan kasvavan noin 28 000:sta yli 45 000:een.

title: Your fries are getting shorter (but no less crispy)
content: No matter what the weather did to this year's harvest, Belgium will still deliver its biggest contribution to the culinary cultural canon: fries. They will still taste good. But this season, the long ones may be missing from your paper cone. First came the potato glut. Last year’s harvest was so abundant that potatoes sold without a contract went for between €0 and €5 per 100 kg – far below production costs, said Daniel Ryckmans, an agronomist at the Walloon potato organisation FIWAP. For this season, the sector asked farmers to plant less, and they did: Belgium's potato fields shrank by 17.4%. Then the summer came, and multiple extreme heatwaves came with it. “This year there was not enough rain. And above that, it was too hot,” Ryckmans told us. The result of this combination is fewer, smaller potatoes. A September assessment by the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU), a non-profit organisation based in the UK, put Belgian yields 21% below their five-year average. At the end of August, only half the Belgian crop of Fontane potatoes, the main frying variety, measured more than 50 mm across. Those are some important millimetres in the potato business. title: French Gov't Cracks Down on Mass Protests over Cost of Living, Education Cuts; 2,400+ Arrested
content:
Hundreds of thousands of protesters marched in over 140 cities across France on Saturday, demanding relief from the high cost of living, more funding for public services and improvements to deteriorating schools, among other grievances. The demonstrations were the latest — and largest — in a series of protests that began in September with high schooler-led demonstrations against overcrowded classrooms and crumbling school infrastructure. Some cities saw property destruction, arson and theft on Saturday, with city halls and other symbols of the state coming under attack. Officials said nearly 1,000 police officers were injured and some 2,400 people were arrested.

“What is frustrating to see is how little the police violence is addressed and talked about, which is really the main violence and the real violence today that is taking place in France,” says Rayyan Seriket, a member of the French student union.

“We’re talking about shattered jaws, high schoolers and adolescents who have been blinded,” adds Harrison Stetler, an independent journalist and teacher based in Paris.

title: EFF Launches Privacy Badger for Safari on macOS
content:

Safari users can download the free browser extension today and join the more than 4 million people using Privacy Badger to take a stand against data brokers and online surveillance. Users will need Safari version 26.5 or higher to use it.

Ranked as one of the best ad tracker blockers by The Wirecutter, Consumer Reports, PC Mag and more, Privacy Badger is different from other blocking extensions. Created by EFF to stop companies from spying on you online, Privacy Badger automatically learns to block hidden trackers on the web, along with additional privacy-protecting features.

title: Roll Call for Freedom: A Ceremony Honoring Political Prisoners
content:
Register 


Around the world, journalists, civic leaders, artists, religious figures, and others are imprisoned for exercising fundamental freedoms. Behind every name is a person whose imprisonment has separated families, silenced vital voices, and deprived communities of courageous leadership.

To mark the International Day of Political Prisoners, Freedom House, the October 30 Coalition, and the National Endowment for Democracy invite the public to gather at the Lincoln Memorial for a ceremony honoring political prisoners and those working for their freedom.

During the event, participants will read the names of prisoners from countries across the world, ensuring that their stories are heard in the heart of the nation’s capital.

The ceremony will also recognize those released during the past year and remember those who died in forced detention. It will conclude with a joint call for free people everywhere to defend the rights of political prisoners, press for their release, and support their families.

title: EU, Belgium, Denmark: Raise Rights With Vietnam’s Leader
content:
(Brussels) – Leaders of the European Union, Belgium, and Denmark should urge Vietnam to make concrete progress in improving its human rights record during Vietnamese President To Lam’s visit to Copenhagen and Brussels the week of October 19-24, 2026, Human Rights Watch said today.

Human Rights Watch wrote to the prime ministers of Denmark and Belgium and, jointly with other groups, to the European Council and European Commission presidents, expressing concerns about Vietnam’s intensifying crackdown on human rights, which violates several obligations and commitments it made to the EU in a 2020 free trade agreement.

“The Vietnamese government has broken its pledges of reform and continues to crack down on basic freedoms,” said Patricia Gossman, senior associate Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “European leaders should communicate clearly and publicly to President To Lam that human rights and labor rights violations will no longer be tolerated.”

title: Ken Paxton’s Anti-Abortion Influence Already Extended Beyond Texas. He Could Take It Further in the Senate.
content:
Early in his tenure as Texas attorney general, Ken Paxton issued a statement commemorating what he believed was a national tragedy.

“It’s impossible to fill the void of more than 50 million missing human beings,” he said in 2016. He was marking the 43rd anniversary of Roe v. Wade, the Supreme Court ruling that protected abortion rights — and had long stood in the way of efforts to ban terminations in early pregnancy, when most abortions occur.

Paxton spent the years that followed testing Roe’s limits and ultimately prevailed where others had failed: In 2021, he defended a near-total abortion ban that Texas legislators had designed to evade conventional legal challenges. The U.S. Supreme Court allowed it to take effect while Roe remained in force.

After the justices overturned Roe the following year, Paxton kept pushing, pursuing new ways to extend the reach of Texas’ restrictions. He prevailed against the Biden administration, picked fights with states that protect abortion access and pioneered strategies that his peers later adopted or expanded.

title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety
content:
The cyberattack last week that hit hundreds of French supermarket refrigerators had Europeans wondering if the nonstop warnings about AI risks had finally landed in the real world.

They hadn’t — at least, not yet.

Experts say the attack, which forced hundreds of retailers to throw away defrosted food and spoiled milk, was mostly a reminder of the importance of old-school cybersecurity in safeguarding essential goods and services.

The attack is a “typical example” of how “low-key cyber-enabled sabotage can affect very crucial supply for society,” said Ferdinand Gehringer, hybrid threats lead at FTI Consulting. 

It’s arguably the most consequential hack in the European Union this year, with tangible, disruptive real-world repercussions. France’s Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu personally managed the fallout, which prompted coordination and information-sharing at the EU level. 

The perpetrators, whose identity and motives are currently unknown, hacked into digital systems to remotely raise the temperature of refrigerators in supermarkets including Intermarché and Carrefour.

title: European businesses are keen to go green
content: The EU has a favourite word: competitiveness. To better compete in the global economy, the European Commission is rewriting (and often weakening) environmental rules for businesses, for example to reduce reporting burdens. Making life easier for our biggest industries sounds reasonable: we shouldn't impose rules that drive them out of business, should we? Yet what do businesses actually want? A recent GlobeScan survey commissioned by the environmental group WWF asked 350 European business leaders. Only 29% said the EU's environmental simplification efforts have helped them, while 55% reported a negative or mixed impact. Meanwhile, 91% said shifting to a low-carbon economy will make Europe more competitive in the long run. Some of that frustration comes from companies that moved towards sustainability first. Many invested in line with the Commission's own green rules, and now feel punished by the uncertainty of changing rules. title: Kenya: Authorities must address economic grievances driving protests, end repressive tactics
content:
Kenyan authorities have increasingly used authoritarian tactics, including arbitrary arrests and detention, abductions, malicious prosecution of protesters, surveillance, and media repression, to crack down on protests against deepening economic hardship and the government’s aggressive fiscal policies, Amnesty International said in a new report today. 

The report, “Human Rights Under Siege: Unpacking Authoritarian Practices in an Era of Economic Pressure amid Youth-Led Protests in Kenya”, documents how between 2023 and 2025, increased food and transport costs, levies and tax hikes, high public debt, corruption, rising poverty and inequality, as well as broken electoral promises led to public anger and protests.

“The findings of this report are troubling and paint a stark picture of the Kenyan government’s repressive response to real grievances affecting the day-to-day lives of ordinary people,” said George Morara, Amnesty International Kenya’s Executive Director.
